\cite{NguyenDang2026}.  Applied to $(2,M)$, dependence is equivalent to $x\in\N$; the
identity
\[
 \gcd(2^n-1,M^n-1)=\gcd(2^n-1,R_0^n-1)
 \quad\text{when }M=2^aR_0, R_0\text{ odd}
\]
shows that the irrelevant common prime-power content disappears.  This is an exact
conditional characterization, not a published proof of the conjecture: no recurrence for
the gcd sequence follows from simultaneous integrality alone.  Together, the gap quotient,
capture cost, and recurrence criterion isolate the missing input as a synchronization
theorem across directions rather than another fixed-ray estimate.

\subsection{Higher Newton--Kummer cocycles and an exponential small algebraic integer}
\label{crit:newton-kummer}

The order-one radical secant from the finite-place analysis extends to a full Newton
hierarchy.  For
$N,m\ge1$, take the positive roots
\[
 P=2^{1/N},\qquad Q=3^{1/N},\qquad
 U=M^{1/N}=P^x,\qquad V=A^{1/N}=Q^x,
\]
and put
\[
 F_m(U,P)=\prod_{j=0}^{m-1}(U-P^j),\qquad
 D_m(P)=F_m(P^m,P).
\]
The cross-base cocycle
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\Xi_{N,m}=F_m(U,P)D_m(Q)-F_m(V,Q)D_m(P)}
 \label{crit:eq-newton-kummer}
\end{equation}
is an algebraic integer.  If
\[
 C_{L,m,N}(y)=\prod_{j=0}^{m-1}
 \frac{e^{yL/N}-e^{jL/N}}{e^{mL/N}-e^{jL/N}},
\]
then in the distinguished real embedding
\begin{equation}
 \Xi_{N,m}=D_m(P)D_m(Q)
 \bigl(C_{\log2,m,N}(x)-C_{\log3,m,N}(x)\bigr).
 \label{crit:eq-newton-kummer-normalized}
\end{equation}
For $m=\lfloor x\rfloor$ and nonintegral $x>m$, each factor
$(q^{x-j}-1)/(q^{m-j}-1)$ is strictly increasing for $q>1$; hence
$\Xi_{N,m}<0$ for every $N$.  For an integral exponent $x=m$, the two normalized products
are both one and $\Xi_{N,m}=0$.  Thus the adaptive cocycle distinguishes the two cases
exactly, although integrality alone does not yet force its vanishing.

For fixed $m$, direct expansion at $N=\infty$ gives
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
 \Xi_{N,m}
 &=\frac{m\,m!}{2}\,x(x-1)\cdots(x-m)
   (\log2\log3)^m(\log2-\log3)N^{-(2m+1)}\\
 &\qquad+O_{x,m}(N^{-(2m+2)}).
\end{split}
 \label{crit:eq-newton-kummer-fixed}
\end{equation}
Order $m=1$ recovers the earlier cubic Kummer determinant.  More importantly, the original
table permits the order to grow.  Write $x=m_0+\delta$ with $0<\delta<1$.  For a prime
$\ell>m_0+1$, shift the solution by
\[
 t_\ell=\ell-1-m_0,\qquad
 (M_{t_\ell},A_{t_\ell})=(2^{t_\ell}M,3^{t_\ell}A),\qquad
 m=\ell-1,\qquad N=\ell,
\]
and denote the resulting cocycle by $\Xi^{(t_\ell)}_{\ell,\ell-1}$.  With
\[
 J(a)=a+\frac{\operatorname{Li}_2(e^{-a})-\pi^2/6}{a},
\]
Euler--Maclaurin for the endpoint products and the gamma-product asymptotic for the
normalized quotient yield
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \lim_{\ell\to\infty}\frac1\ell
 \log\left|\Xi^{(t_\ell)}_{\ell,\ell-1}\right|
 =J(\log2)+J(\log3)
 =-0.9053250970927727\ldots .}
 \label{crit:eq-newton-kummer-shifted}
\end{equation}
This is the first exponentially small algebraic integer supplied by the fixed-table Kummer
construction.  Genuine integer exponents instead make every adaptive shifted cocycle exactly
zero.

The natural algebraic operations nevertheless lose the cancellation.  Put
\[
 \rho=\operatorname{rank}_{\Z}\langle2,3,M,A\rangle\in\{3,4\}.
\]
For primes outside the fixed saturation index, the pure-radical field
\[
 K_\ell=\Q(2^{1/\ell},3^{1/\ell},M^{1/\ell},A^{1/\ell})
\]
has degree $\ell^\rho$.  Every conjugate of the shifted cocycle is
$\exp(O(\ell))$, so the elementary norm bound reaches only
\begin{equation}
 \left|\Xi^{(t_\ell)}_{\ell,\ell-1}\right|
 \ge \exp\bigl(-O(\ell^{\rho+1})\bigr),
 \label{crit:eq-newton-kummer-norm-gap}
\end{equation}
far below the linear exponential scale in~\eqref{crit:eq-newton-kummer-shifted}.

Ordinary traces are worse.  Let
$F=\Q(\zeta_\ell,P,Q)$, $S=m(m-1)/2$, and take $m<\ell$.  For every sufficiently large good
prime, rank four gives
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{Tr}_{F(U,V)/F}(\Xi_{\ell,m})
 =\ell^2(-1)^m\bigl(P^SD_m(Q)-Q^SD_m(P)\bigr).
 \label{crit:eq-newton-kummer-trace-four}
\end{equation}
In the non-axis rank-three branch write $U=cW^r$, $V=dW^s$ over $F$; for good
$\ell\nmid rs$,
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{Tr}_{F(W)/F}(\Xi_{\ell,m})
 =\ell(-1)^m\bigl(P^SD_m(Q)-Q^SD_m(P)\bigr).
 \label{crit:eq-newton-kummer-trace-three}
\end{equation}
Character orthogonality has erased $M,A,x$ completely.  At $m=\ell-1$ the dominant base-only
term grows like $\exp(0.281244\ldots\ell)$, so trace destroys precisely the distinguished
cancellation.  This is not an accident of the invariant character: writing
$F_m(T,P)=\sum_{k=0}^mc_k(P)T^k$, every rank-four character projection of $\Xi$ is either
the base-only constant term, one term $D_m(Q)c_k(P)U^k$, or one term
$-D_m(P)c_k(Q)V^k$.  All mixed nonconstant characters vanish.  Linear Fourier projection
therefore either erases both outputs or retains only one axis; the rank-three exception is
exactly a support collision forced by its unique relation.

There is one useful rank calibration.  If $\gcd(6,MA)=1$, then the base-prime and output-prime
valuation lattices split.  Rank three would force $M=W^r$, $A=W^s$, hence
$\log_2 3=s/r\in\Q$, impossible.  Every hypothetical cross-coprime counterexample is
therefore in the harder rank-four Kummer branch.  The natural common ideal can be computed
exactly, and it is still too small.  Let $\ell>3$ be prime, $1\le m<\ell$, put
$P=2^{1/\ell}$, $Q=3^{1/\ell}$, $L=\Q(P,Q)$, and write
\[
 S=\frac{m(m-1)}2,\qquad
 H_a(m)=\prod_{r=1}^m(a^r-1),\qquad
 D_m(P)=P^S\prod_{r=1}^m(P^r-1)
\]
with the analogous formula for $D_m(Q)$.  For the ideal
\begin{equation}
 \mathfrak I_{\ell,m}=(D_m(P))+(D_m(Q))\subset\mathcal O_L,
 \label{crit:eq-newton-kummer-ideal}
\end{equation}
set $a_p=v_p(H_2(m))$ and $b_p=v_p(H_3(m))$.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 N_{L/\Q}\mathfrak I_{\ell,m}
 =6^S\ell^{e_{\ell,m}}
   \prod_{p\nmid6\ell}p^{\min(a_p,b_p)},
 \qquad
 0\le e_{\ell,m}\le\ell\min(a_\ell,b_\ell).}
 \label{crit:eq-newton-kummer-ideal-norm}
\end{equation}
At a good prime, a prime ideal dividing $D_m(P)$ makes $P^r=1$ for some $r<\ell$.
B\'ezout between $r$ and $\ell$ then puts $P$ in the prime field and determines it uniquely
from $2$; the same holds for $Q$.  Hence exactly one common degree-one prime occurs, with
valuation $\min(a_p,b_p)$.  The primes $2$ and $3$ contribute $2^S$ and $3^S$; the displayed
bound at $\ell$ follows from the two principal norms and LTE.  In particular
\begin{equation}
 \log N_{L/\Q}\mathfrak I_{\ell,m}=O(m^2+m\ell)=O(\ell^2).
 \label{crit:eq-newton-kummer-ideal-size}
\end{equation}
For fixed $m$ and all sufficiently large $\ell$, the exact norm is simply
$6^S\gcd(H_2(m),H_3(m))$.

This settles the partial-norm scale.  The cross-resultants give
\[
 |N_{L/\Q}D_m(P)|=(2^SH_2(m))^\ell,
 \qquad
 |N_{L/\Q}D_m(Q)|=(3^SH_3(m))^\ell.
\]
In Kummer rank $\rho$, extension to $K_\ell$ raises
\eqref{crit:eq-newton-kummer-ideal-norm} to the power $\ell^{\rho-2}$.  At
$m=\ell-1$ its logarithm is therefore only $O(\ell^\rho)$, one full factor of $\ell$
below the $O(\ell^{\rho+1})$ conjugate cost in
\eqref{crit:eq-newton-kummer-norm-gap}.  In the cyclotomic Kummer closure, taking a norm over
any subgroup of the output-twist group multiplies the ideal power and divides the remaining
field degree in inverse proportions, so the absolute deficit is unchanged.  Projective
normalization does not repair it either:
\begin{equation}
 (D_m(P))\cap(D_m(Q))=(D_m(P)D_m(Q))\mathfrak I_{\ell,m}^{-1},
 \qquad
 \log N_{L/\Q}\bigl((D_m(P))\cap(D_m(Q))\bigr)
 =\ell^3\log6+O(\ell^2)
 \label{crit:eq-newton-kummer-projective-tax}
\end{equation}
when $m=\ell-1$.  The normalized cross-base difference in
\eqref{crit:eq-newton-kummer-normalized} is only polynomial at this shifted order; the
exponential smallness comes from the distinguished values of $D_m(P)D_m(Q)$, exactly where
the projective denominator is largest.  Thus ordinary traces, character projections, ideal
gcds, and subgroup output partial norms do not improve these bounds at their exact scales.
A signed group-ring operation faces a sharper integrality obstruction.  Continue in the
good rank-four branch over $F=\Q(\zeta_\ell,P,Q)$ and write
\[
 \mathcal A_a=D_m(Q)F_m(\zeta_\ell^aU,P),\qquad
 \mathcal B_b=D_m(P)F_m(\zeta_\ell^bV,Q),\qquad
 \mathcal X_{a,b}=\mathcal A_a-\mathcal B_b.
\]
The output-twist group $G\simeq\mathbf F_\ell^2$ translates the two indices.  Its smallest mixed
additive projection vanishes identically,
\[
 \mathcal X_{0,0}-\mathcal X_{1,0}-\mathcal X_{0,1}+\mathcal X_{1,1}=0,
\]
whereas the corresponding multiplicative operation, wherever defined, is the genuine
cross-ratio
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal C=
 \frac{\mathcal X_{0,0}\mathcal X_{1,1}}
      {\mathcal X_{1,0}\mathcal X_{0,1}},
 \qquad
 N_{F(U,V)/F}(\mathcal C)=1,
 \qquad
 \mathcal C-1=
 \frac{(\mathcal A_0-\mathcal A_1)(\mathcal B_0-\mathcal B_1)}
      {\mathcal X_{1,0}\mathcal X_{0,1}}.
 \label{crit:eq-signed-kummer-cross-ratio}
\end{equation}
Thus an integral $\mathcal C$ would necessarily be a unit; otherwise it pays exactly the
displayed denominator.  Clearing that denominator leaves a product of one-axis differences
and loses the distinguished cross-base subtraction.  After specializing the formal
cross-ratio to an integral rank-collapsed calibration with $\mathcal X_{0,0}=0$ and nonzero
denominator, $\mathcal C-1=-1$, not a small residual.

More generally, for $\Theta=\sum_{g\in G}n_gg\in\Z[G]$ and
$\mathcal X=\mathcal X_{0,0}$,
\begin{equation}
 v_{\mathfrak p}(\mathcal X^\Theta)
 =\sum_gn_gv_{g^{-1}\mathfrak p}(\mathcal X),\qquad
 N_{F(U,V)/F}(\mathcal X^\Theta)
 =N_{F(U,V)/F}(\mathcal X)^{\operatorname{aug}\Theta}.
 \label{crit:eq-signed-kummer-divisor}
\end{equation}
These are the exact divisor-convolution and augmentation tests.  Zero augmentation plus
integrality forces a unit.  If a prime divisor of $\mathcal X$ has a free private
$G$-orbit, the first formula forces every $n_g\ge0$; zero augmentation then forces
$\Theta=0$, while positive augmentation retains ordinary norm mass.  Establishing such a
private prime for the primitive part of $\mathcal X$ would require a new
cross-conjugate primitive-divisor theorem.

The missing statement has an exact resultant form.  Let
$\mathfrak J=\mathfrak I_{\ell,m}\mathcal O_F$,
$\mathfrak a=(\mathcal X_{0,0})(\mathfrak J\mathcal O_{F(U,V)})^{-1}$, and
\[
 \Phi_A(T)=\prod_{a\in\mathbf F_\ell}(T-\mathcal A_a),\qquad
 \Phi_B(T)=\prod_{b\in\mathbf F_\ell}(T-\mathcal B_b).
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 R_{\ell,m}:=\operatorname{Res}(\Phi_A,\Phi_B)
 =N_{F(U,V)/F}(\mathcal X_{0,0}),\qquad
 N_{F(U,V)/F}\mathfrak a=(R_{\ell,m})\mathfrak J^{-\ell^2}.
 \label{crit:eq-private-prime-resultant}
\end{equation}
Choose a nonzero submaximal minor $S_{\ell,m}$ of the Sylvester matrix.  If a prime dividing
the primitive ideal on the right avoids ramification, $\mathfrak J$, the two discriminants,
and $S_{\ell,m}$, then the reduced orbit polynomials have a separable gcd of degree one.
The unique common pair is Frobenius-fixed, so the prime splits in both output directions and
gives a free private divisor of one conjugate difference.  Thus absence of a private prime
confines the radical of the primitive resultant to this explicit exceptional product.
This criterion does not prove existence: the available bounds for the logarithms of the
absolute norms of both the resultant and the discriminant--minor product are
$O_x(\ell^5)$ for fixed $m$ and $O_x(\ell^6)$ for $m=\ell-1$.  A squarefree divisor outside this potentially
same-scale exceptional factor is precisely the missing arithmetic input.

At $m=1$ that missing input has a particularly explicit form.  Put
$d_2=P-1$, $d_3=Q-1$, $c=P-Q$, $\mu=d_3^\ell M$, and
$\nu=d_2^\ell A$.  Shifting the exponent from $x$ to $x+t$ replaces the resultant by
\[
 R_t=\mathcal C_\ell(2^t\mu,3^t\nu;c),\qquad
 \mathcal C_\ell(X,Y;c)
 =\operatorname{Res}_z(z^\ell-X,(z+c)^\ell-Y).
\]
The curve $\mathcal C_\ell=0$ is the irreducible rational image
$z\mapsto(z^\ell,(z+c)^\ell)$.  Away from a fixed finite set $\mathcal S_\ell$ of primes,
its only torus singularities are the finitely many ordinary double points
\[
 (X,Y)=c^\ell\left(
  \left(\frac{\zeta_\ell^b-1}{\zeta_\ell^a-\zeta_\ell^b}\right)^\ell,
  \left(\frac{\zeta_\ell^a-1}{\zeta_\ell^a-\zeta_\ell^b}\right)^\ell
 \right),\qquad a,b\in\mathbf F_\ell^\times,\ a\ne b.
\]
Corvaja--Zannier~\cite{CorvajaZannier2005} bounds the radical supported at this finite node
locus by $\exp(o(t))$.  The complementary radical has a standard conditional lower bound,
rather than requiring a separate truncated-radical hypothesis.  Take
$K=F=\Q(\zeta_\ell,P,Q)$, which contains the coefficients and all nodes, put
$D=[K:\Q]$, and enlarge
$\mathcal S_\ell$ to contain every prime above $6\ell c\mu\nu$ together with the fixed
coefficient and bad-reduction primes.  Let $h_K$ denote the absolute logarithmic projective
height normalized by $D^{-1}$, and write
\[
 \operatorname{rad}_K(\alpha)
 =\frac1D\sum_{\mathfrak q\mid(\alpha)}\log N\mathfrak q
 \qquad(0\ne\alpha\in\mathcal O_K),
\]
while $\operatorname{rad}_K(a:b:r)$ is $D^{-1}$ times the sum of $\log N\mathfrak q$
over primes at which $v_{\mathfrak q}(a),v_{\mathfrak q}(b),v_{\mathfrak q}(r)$ are not all
equal.
For odd $\ell$ set $W=X-Y+c^\ell$.  There is a polynomial
$G_\ell\in\Z[X,Y,Z]$, homogeneous of degree $\ell-3$, such that
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\mathcal C_\ell(X,Y;c)
 =W^\ell+c^\ell XYG_\ell(X,Y,c^\ell).}
 \label{crit:eq-private-prime-fermat-splitting}
\end{equation}
Indeed, $\mathcal C_\ell$ and $W^\ell$ agree when $X=0$, $Y=0$, or $c=0$.
Moreover $\mathcal C_\ell$ is invariant under $c\mapsto\zeta_\ell c$ and is weighted
homogeneous of weight $\ell^2$ when $X,Y,c$ have weights $\ell,\ell,1$.  Their difference is
therefore divisible in $\Z[X,Y,c]$ by $XYc^\ell$, and the quotient has the asserted integral
homogeneity.  Irreducibility of $\mathcal C_\ell$ gives
\[
 \gcd\bigl(X-Y+Z,G_\ell(X,Y,Z)\bigr)=1.
\]
Homogeneity and $c\ne0$ preserve this coprimality after the specialization $Z=c^\ell$;
this is the coprime pair used below.

Put $W_t=2^t\mu-3^t\nu+c^\ell$ and
$G_t=G_\ell(2^t\mu,3^t\nu,c^\ell)$.  Outside $\mathcal S_\ell$, the common
ideal of $W_t^\ell$ and $c^\ell2^t3^t\mu\nu G_t$ has local order
\[
 \min\{\ell v_{\mathfrak q}(W_t),v_{\mathfrak q}(G_t)\}
 \le \ell\min\{v_{\mathfrak q}(W_t),v_{\mathfrak q}(G_t)\},
\]
so Corvaja--Zannier gives logarithmic norm $o(t)$.  The same estimate at the finitely many
primes in $\mathcal S_\ell$ follows by applying the fixed-$S$ theorem of
Bugeaud--Evertse~\cite{BugeaudEvertse2017} to the simple nondegenerate integer recurrence
$N_{K/\Q}(W_t)$.  Its support contains the root $1$, so no rational prime divides all of its
recurrence coefficients, and its fixed-$S$ part is $\exp(o(t))$.  With projective radicals
normalized by $D^{-1}$ as above, this gives
\begin{align}
 h_K\bigl(W_t^\ell:c^\ell2^t3^t\mu\nu G_t:R_t\bigr)
   &=\ell t\log3+o(t),\nonumber\\
 \operatorname{rad}_K(W_t)&\le t\log3+O(1),\nonumber\\
 \operatorname{rad}_K(G_t)&\le(\ell-3)t\log3+O(1),
 \label{crit:eq-private-prime-abc-inputs}
\end{align}
while $2^t3^t\mu\nu c$ has fixed radical.  The number-field $abc$ conjecture over this fixed
$K$, in the form
\[
 h_K(a:b:a+b)
 \le(1+\varepsilon)\operatorname{rad}_K(a:b:a+b)+O_{K,\varepsilon}(1),
\]
therefore gives
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{rad}_K(R_t)
 \ge\left(\frac{\ell}{1+\varepsilon}-(\ell-2)\right)t\log3-o(t).
 \label{crit:eq-private-prime-abc-radical}
\end{equation}
Consequently, conditionally on number-field $abc$, for every $\delta>0$,
\[
 \operatorname{rad}_K(R_t)\ge(2\log3-\delta)t
\]
for all sufficiently large $t$.  The node-supported radical is $o(t)$, so a divisor remains
at a smooth point.  Its unique normalization preimage is Frobenius-fixed and, in the good
full rank-four branch, gives a free private prime for one conjugate difference.  Thus no
nontrivial integral augmentation-zero operation exists for any sufficiently large shifted
$m=1$ instance at that fixed $\ell$.

For $\ell=3$ the splitting is the concrete identity
\[
 \mathcal C_3(X,Y;c)=(X-Y+c^3)^3+27c^3XY.
\]
Away from the structural primes, its unique torus singularity is the ordinary node
$(c^3,-c^3)$.  This checks the sign, the coefficient $G_3=27$, and the absence of moving
common content in the second summand.  Unconditionally, $N_{K/\Q}(R_t)$ is a simple
nondegenerate integer recurrence with a unique dominant root, but Stewart's general
squarefree-factor estimate gives only
\[
 \log\operatorname{rad}_{\Q}|N_{K/\Q}(R_t)|
 \gg_{K,\ell,\mu,\nu,c}
 \frac{\log t\,\log\log t}{\log\log\log t}
 \qquad\text{\cite{Stewart2008Squarefree}},
\]
which is $o(t)$ and does not dominate the $o(t)$ node bound.  Classical Zsigmondy theorems
do not apply to this nonbinary, nondivisibility recurrence.

The conclusion uses the full output-twist group.  Shifting multiplies $U,V$ by
$P^t,Q^t\in F$, so it leaves the Kummer extension and its saturation unchanged.  For an
integral control $x=k$, however, $U=P^k$ and $V=Q^k$ already lie in $F$; the output extension
collapses, the formal resultant is not an $\ell^2$-degree Galois norm, and a smooth divisor
supplies no free output orbit.  The same caveat applies at a bad rank-collapsed prime
$\ell$.  The fixed-$\ell$ conditional result is not uniform in $\ell$ and reaches neither
the original unshifted instance nor the adaptive $m=\ell-1$ cocycle.

These two failures are structural.  First, the coefficient supplied by
\eqref{crit:eq-private-prime-abc-radical} is
\[
 c_\ell(\varepsilon)
 =\frac{\ell}{1+\varepsilon}-(\ell-2)
 =2-\frac{\ell\varepsilon}{1+\varepsilon}.
\]
It is positive only for $\varepsilon<2/(\ell-2)$; obtaining
$c_\ell(\varepsilon)\ge2-\delta$ for $0<\delta<2$ requires
$\varepsilon\le\delta/(\ell-\delta)$.  Thus even a field-uniform $abc$ estimate with one
fixed $\varepsilon$ cannot be diagonalized.  At the adaptive shift
$t_\ell=\ell-1-\lfloor x\rfloor$, one would need
$\varepsilon_\ell=O(\ell^{-1})$ and every fixed-field $abc$, gcd, and fixed-prime-part
error to be $o(\ell)$.  The Bugeaud--Evertse threshold used above is not uniform in $\ell$, while
\[
 h(\mu),h(\nu)=\Theta_x(\ell),\qquad
 \log\lVert G_\ell\rVert_\infty=O(\ell^2),
\]
so the fixed-$\ell$ asymptotic has no such diagonal error term.

Second, order one does not divide the higher Newton hierarchy.  On its normalized
common-zero curve write
\[
 U=1+\sigma(P-1),\qquad V=1+\sigma(Q-1),\qquad
 \mathcal T_{P,m}(\sigma)
 =\frac{F_m(1+\sigma(P-1),P)}{D_m(P)}.
\]
For every $m\ge2$, the difference
$\mathcal T_{P,m}(\sigma)-\mathcal T_{Q,m}(\sigma)$ is a nonzero polynomial.  Already
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal T_{P,2}(\sigma)-\mathcal T_{Q,2}(\sigma)
 =\sigma(\sigma-1)
 \left(\frac1{P(P+1)}-\frac1{Q(Q+1)}\right),
 \label{crit:eq-newton-order-separation}
\end{equation}
and in general its leading coefficient is
\[
 \frac{P^{-m(m-1)/2}}
      {\prod_{r=1}^m(1+P+\cdots+P^{r-1})}
 -
 \frac{Q^{-m(m-1)/2}}
      {\prod_{r=1}^m(1+Q+\cdots+Q^{r-1})}\ne0
\]
for $1<P<Q$.  A private divisor of an order-one difference therefore has no systematic
reason to divide the order-$(\ell-1)$ cocycle.  There is no polynomial-factor descent in the
shift parameter either: for distinct $r,t$ the irreducible polynomials
\[
 \mathcal C_\ell(2^rX,3^rY;c)
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \mathcal C_\ell(2^tX,3^tY;c)
\]
are coprime.  Their common constant term fixes any associate scalar, and their $X^\ell$
coefficients then force $r=t$.

Finally, the free-orbit conclusion exists only in rank four; rank three remains an unresolved
branch under the hypothetical counterexample.  At adaptive order in rank four, the absolute resultant and its
discriminant--minor exceptional factor both have logarithmic size $O_x(\ell^6)$, whereas
the known common ideal contributes only $O_x(\ell^5)$.  The diagonalized order-one $abc$
lower bound has unnormalized scale $\Theta_x(\ell^4)$ and, by
\eqref{crit:eq-newton-order-separation}, concerns a different resultant.  The exact
missing input is therefore a moving-family truncated primitive-divisor theorem for the
order-$(\ell-1)$ Kummer resultants, together with a separate rank-three analysis; standard
fixed-field $abc$ does not provide either one.

The extracted common ideal $\mathfrak I_{\ell,m}$ cancels from every
augmentation-zero ratio.  Multiplication by
cyclotomic units does not change valuations, and a Stickelberger class-group annihilator
can principalize the resulting fractional ideal without removing its negative valuations.
Consequently a successful algebraic operation must create exceptional cross-conjugate ideal
overlap; changing the group-ring element alone cannot preserve the signed cancellation as an
algebraic integer.

The product/cocycle identities and integral-exponent calibrations are \statuslean{} in
\lean{RankOneNewtonKummer}.  The finite signed-orbit augmentation identity, mixed additive
cancellation, and two-by-two minor factorization are \statuslean{} in
\lean{SignedOrbitNormFinite}; the divisor, integrality, private-prime, asymptotic,
Kummer-degree, norm, ideal, and trace analyses are paper mathematics.  The resultant
splitting~\eqref{crit:eq-private-prime-fermat-splitting} and its local consequences are
unconditional paper results; the linear radical and resulting private prime use the
number-field $abc$ conjecture explicitly.

\subsection{Adjacent-smooth cyclic resultants and finite-logarithm descent}
\label{crit:adjacent-resultants}

The four adjacent smooth pairs identified in Section~\ref{mom:moments} support a Kummer
construction whose distinguished embedding has unit rather than
exponential scale.  Let $N/q<x$ be a reduced lower convergent, put
$\varepsilon=qx-N>0$ and $s=qx/N=1+\varepsilon/N$, and for
$a\in\{1,2,3,8\}$ set
\[
 P_a=a^{qx},\qquad Q_a=(a+1)^{qx},\qquad
 u_a=P_a^{1/N}=a^s,\qquad v_a=Q_a^{1/N}=(a+1)^s.
\]
All $P_a,Q_a$ are integers under a hypothetical solution.

For arbitrary positive integers $P<Q$, let
$\alpha=(Q/P)^{1/N}$, $\zeta_N=e^{2\pi i/N}$, and
\[
 Z_j=P(\zeta_N^j\alpha-1)^N\qquad(0\le j<N).
\]
The distinguished value $Z_0$ lies in the pure-radical field $\Q(\alpha)$ of degree at most
$N$.  The other $Z_j$ generally do not; they lie in
$\Q(\zeta_N,\alpha)$, whose Kummer splitting extension over $\Q(\zeta_N)$ is cyclic of
degree dividing $N$.  Nevertheless the complete multiset is Galois-stable, and
\begin{equation}
 \Phi_{N;P,Q}(T)
 :=\prod_{j=0}^{N-1}(T-Z_j)
 =P^{-N}\operatorname{Res}_X(PX^N-Q,T-P(X-1)^N)
 \in\Z[T].
 \label{crit:eq-adjacent-universal-polynomial}
\end{equation}
This is a degree-$N$ characteristic/resultant polynomial, not necessarily the minimal
polynomial of an individual $Z_j$.  Its power sums are
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{j=0}^{N-1}Z_j^m
 =N\sum_{r=0}^{m}\binom{Nm}{Nr}
   (-1)^{N(m-r)}P^{m-r}Q^r.
 \label{crit:eq-adjacent-power-sums}
\end{equation}
Define the integer
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal R_N(P,Q)=\prod_{j=0}^{N-1}(Z_j-1)
 =(-1)^N\Phi_{N;P,Q}(1).
 \label{crit:eq-cyclic-catalan-resultant}
\end{equation}
For the adjacent data this integer is positive: the distinguished factor is positive,
nonreal factors pair with their conjugates, and
$|\zeta_N^jv_a-u_a|\ge v_a-u_a>1$ excludes a zero factor.

Let
\[
 c_a=(a+1)\log(a+1)-a\log a.
\]
The distinguished defect has the scale-free expansion
\begin{equation}
 (v_a-u_a)^N-1
 =c_a\varepsilon+\frac{c_a^2}{2}\varepsilon^2
 +O_a(\varepsilon^2/N+|\varepsilon|^3).
 \label{crit:eq-adjacent-distinguished-jet}
\end{equation}
For the remaining embeddings, exact factorization and a Gaussian boundary layer give
\begin{align}
 \mathcal R_N(P_a,Q_a)
 &=(Q_a-P_a)^N\prod_{j=0}^{N-1}
   |1-(\zeta_N^jv_a-u_a)^{-N}|,\nonumber\\
 \log\mathcal R_N(P_a,Q_a)
 &=N\log(Q_a-P_a)+\log(c_a\varepsilon)
   -\gamma_a\sqrt N+o(\sqrt N),\nonumber\\
 \gamma_a&=\frac{\zeta(3/2)}{\sqrt{2\pi a(a+1)}}.
 \label{crit:eq-adjacent-boundary-law}
\end{align}
The Riemann-sum proof is uniform on
$\delta\sqrt N\le j\le L\sqrt N$; the singular initial window is dominated first, then
$\delta\downarrow0$, and the Gaussian tail is removed after $L\uparrow\infty$.  Uniform
convergence all the way down to $j=1$ is neither needed nor true in general.

Write $\mathcal R_a=\mathcal R_N(P_a,Q_a)$.  Cancellation of both $N^2$ height components
and of $\log\varepsilon$ has, up to sign, the unique primitive weight vector
\[
 (w_1,w_2,w_3,w_8)=(2,-2,-1,1).
\]
Thus
\begin{equation}
 \Theta_{N,q}=\frac{\mathcal R_1^2\mathcal R_8}
 {\mathcal R_3\mathcal R_2^2}
 =C_0\exp(-\kappa\sqrt N+o(\sqrt N)),
 \label{crit:eq-balanced-catalan-quotient}
\end{equation}
where
\begin{align}
 C_0&=\frac{c_1^2c_8}{c_3c_2^2}
 =0.7356241567479139\ldots,\nonumber\\
 \kappa&=2\gamma_1+\gamma_8-\gamma_3-2\gamma_2
 =0.44490230205040846\ldots>0.
 \label{crit:eq-balanced-catalan-constants}
\end{align}
If $\Theta_{N,q}=U_{N,q}/V_{N,q}$ is reduced, positivity of the numerator forces
\begin{equation}
 \liminf\frac{\log V_{N,q}}{\sqrt N}\ge\kappa.
 \label{crit:eq-balanced-denominator}
\end{equation}
Consequently the conjecture would follow from any fixed $\eta>0$ and infinitely many lower
convergents for which
\[
 \frac{\mathcal R_3\mathcal R_2^2}
 {\gcd(\mathcal R_1^2\mathcal R_8,\mathcal R_3\mathcal R_2^2)}
 \le e^{(\kappa-\eta)\sqrt N}.
\]
This makes the required cross-specialization gcd cancellation exact; it does not prove it.

The same four pairs have an exact tangent lattice.  For $U=2^s$, $V=3^s$, put
\[
 e_1=U-2,\quad e_2=V-U-1,\quad
 e_3=U^2-V-1,\quad e_8=V^2-U^3-1.
\]
Then
\begin{align}
 -3e_1+e_2+e_3&=e_1^2,\nonumber\\
 6e_1-6e_2+e_8&=-e_1^3-5e_1^2+2e_1e_2+e_2^2,
 \label{crit:eq-catalan-tangent-identities}
\end{align}
and all integer relations among $(c_1,c_2,c_3,c_8)$ form
\begin{equation}
 \Z(-3,1,1,0)\oplus\Z(6,-6,0,1).
 \label{crit:eq-catalan-tangent-lattice}
\end{equation}
Every nonzero vector has support at least three, and those directions span the rank-two
Kummer lattice.  This exact support statement alone does not prove that cancellation cannot
occur in a degree-$N$ subfield; that stronger claim would require a separate
Kummer-character argument.

At a prime degree $\ell$, Frobenius supplies a conditional finite-place shadow.  In
$\mathbb F_\ell[P,Q,T]$,
\begin{equation}
 \Phi_{\ell;P,Q}(T)\equiv(T-Q+P)^\ell.
 \label{crit:eq-catalan-frobenius-collapse}
\end{equation}
If $\ell\nmid P$ and $Q-P-1=\ell C$, put
\[
 H_\ell(X)=\frac{(X-1)^\ell-X^\ell+1}{\ell}\in\Z[X].
\]
Then $\ell^\ell\mid\mathcal R_\ell(P,Q)$ and, for $r=Q/P$ modulo $\ell$,
\begin{equation}
 \frac{\mathcal R_\ell(P,Q)}{\ell^\ell}
 \equiv PH_\ell(r)+C,\qquad
 H_\ell(X)\equiv\sum_{k=1}^{\ell-1}\frac{X^k}{k}\pmod\ell.
 \label{crit:eq-catalan-first-frobenius}
\end{equation}
Now impose the additional simultaneous resonance
$M^q\equiv2$ and $A^q\equiv3\pmod\ell$, and write
$M^q=2+\ell\xi$, $A^q=3+\ell\upsilon$ modulo $\ell^2$.  The four normalized first
quotients $W_a=\mathcal R_a/\ell^\ell\bmod\ell$ are
\begin{align}
 W_1&=-2q_\ell(2)+\xi,\nonumber\\
 W_2&=2q_\ell(2)-3q_\ell(3)+\upsilon-\xi,\nonumber\\
 W_3&=-8q_\ell(2)+3q_\ell(3)+4\xi-\upsilon,\nonumber\\
 W_8&=24q_\ell(2)-18q_\ell(3)+6\upsilon-12\xi.
 \label{crit:eq-catalan-four-residues}
\end{align}
They obey the same two tangent relations as
\eqref{crit:eq-catalan-tangent-lattice}.  If all four are nonzero and
$t=W_2/W_1$, the balanced residual collapses to
\begin{equation}
 \Theta_{\ell,q}\equiv\frac{6(t-1)}{t^2(3-t)}\pmod\ell.
 \label{crit:eq-catalan-residual-map}
\end{equation}
The resonance is not known to occur infinitely often.  The finite tangent identities,
conditional balance and tangent-lattice parametrizations, two residue relations, and a
conditional residual cross identity are \statuslean{} in \lean{CatalanTangentCore}.  The
universal polynomial, boundary law,
balanced quotient, and conditional Frobenius formulas are \statusnew{} paper results.
They replace a generic Kummer-height loss by a sharply specified cross-resultant gcd and
finite-logarithm problem, but do not yet close either one.

\subsection{Common-zero Hermite jets stop at order two}
\label{crit:hermite}

The common-zero route admits a striking but non-closing normalization.  For $a>1$ put
\begin{equation}
 F_a(z)=\frac{a^{-z/2}\sin(\pi a^z)}{\pi\log a}.
 \label{crit:eq-half-density}
\end{equation}
At a positive zero $\lambda$ with $m=a^\lambda\in\N$ one has
\begin{equation}
 F_a'(\lambda)=(-1)^m\sqrt m\in\Qbar,
 \qquad F_a''(\lambda)=0.
 \label{crit:eq-algebraic-jet}
\end{equation}
Hence at a common zero, with $u=2^\lambda$ and $v=3^\lambda$, the removable quotient
$H=F_2/F_3$ satisfies
\[
 H(\lambda)=(-1)^{u-v}\sqrt{u/v}\in\Qbar,
 \qquad H'(\lambda)=0.
\]
This algebraic first jet adds no new logarithmic direction because $H(\lambda)^2=u/v$.

The next two normalized jets make the ceiling exact.  With $L=\log a$,
\begin{equation}
 r_3:=\frac{F_a'''(\lambda)}{F_a'(\lambda)}
 =L^2\left(\frac14-\pi^2m^2\right),\qquad
 r_4:=\frac{F_a''''(\lambda)}{F_a'(\lambda)}=-4\pi^2L^3m^2,
 \label{crit:eq-higher-jets}
\end{equation}
and therefore
\begin{equation}
 L^3-4r_3L+r_4=0.
 \label{crit:eq-jet-cubic}
\end{equation}
The two higher jets cannot both be algebraic: the cubic would first make $L$ algebraic, and
then the formula for the nonzero $r_4$ would make $\pi^2$ algebraic, contrary to
Lindemann--Weierstrass~\cite{Baker1975}.

The extra multiplicity in the unit-shift defect is paid exactly by an explicit
infinite-order multiplier.  Writing $c_2(z)=\cos(\pi2^z)$,
$c_3(z)=\cos(\pi3^z)$ and
\[
 B_1(z)=3c_2(z)-4c_3(z)^2+1,
\]
one has at every common zero $\lambda=n+k\beta$ with $n,k\ge1$
\begin{equation}
 F_2(z+1)F_3(z)-\sqrt{2/3}\,F_2(z)F_3(z+1)
 =\frac{\sqrt2}{3}F_2(z)F_3(z)B_1(z).
 \label{crit:eq-hermite-defect}
\end{equation}
Here $B_1$ has an exact double zero, so the cleared defect has order four, but $B_1$ is of
infinite order.  The quotient $F_2/F_3$ also has at least $3^R-2^R+O(1)$ nonshared real poles
up to real part $R$, and is not of bounded characteristic in the right half-plane.  Thus the algebraic first jet does
not feed Schneider--Lang, a finite-order argument, or a bounded-characteristic uniqueness
theorem; third derivatives restore the original logarithmic obstruction.

\subsection{Lambert universality and the reciprocal-Hankel universal-clearing deficit}
\label{crit:lambert-hankel}

Over a field, for parameters $(s,r)$ satisfying $s^n\ne1$ for every $n\ge1$, define
\[
 h_n(s,r)=\frac{r^n-1}{s^n-1},\qquad
 \mathcal H_{s,r}(X)=\sum_{n\ge1}h_n(s,r)X^n,
\]
and let $\Delta_cG(X)=G(cX)-G(X)$.  Coefficientwise cancellation gives
\begin{equation}
 \Delta_s\mathcal H_{s,r}
 =\frac{rX}{1-rX}-\frac{X}{1-X}=:R_r(X).
 \label{crit:eq-lambert-cocycle}
\end{equation}
More importantly,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \Delta_N\Delta_2\mathcal H_{2,M}
 =\Delta_M\Delta_3\mathcal H_{3,N}}
 \label{crit:eq-universal-double-cocycle}
\end{equation}
holds for arbitrary rational $M,N$; both sides have $n$th coefficient
$(M^n-1)(N^n-1)$.  Thus this visually cross-base identity contains no common-exponent input.
The exact formal-series algebra, including the rational presentation and the fully generic
four-parameter identity, is \statuslean{} in \lean{LambertCocycleFinite}.

The leading Hankel determinants of the same sequence are also exact.  Put
\[
 \mathcal D_n(s,r)=\det\left(\frac{r^{i+j+1}-1}{s^{i+j+1}-1}
                       \right)_{0\le i,j<n}.
\]
The Cauchy double alternant and the rank drops at $r=1,s^{\pm1},\ldots,s^{\pm(n-1)}$
give
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
 \mathcal D_n(s,r)
 &=(-1)^{\binom n2}s^{\binom n3}(r-1)^n\\
 &\quad\times
 \frac{\displaystyle\prod_{k=1}^{n-1}
 (s^k-r)^{n-k}(s^kr-1)^{n-k}(s^k-1)^{2(n-k)}}
 {\displaystyle\prod_{i,j=0}^{n-1}(s^{i+j+1}-1)}.
\end{split}
 \label{crit:eq-hankel-product}
\end{equation}
For integer $s,r\ge2$, the universal cyclotomic integerizer
\[
 Q_n(s)=
 \frac{\prod_{i,j<n}(s^{i+j+1}-1)}
      {\prod_{k=1}^{n-1}(s^k-1)^{2(n-k)}}
\]
is an integer.  Off the locus $r=s^k$ one has
\begin{align}
 \log Q_n(s)&=\frac23n^3\log s+O_s(n),
 \label{crit:eq-hankel-denominator}\\
 \log|\mathcal D_n(s,r)|
 &=-\frac16n^3\log s+\frac12n^2\log(r/s)+O_{s,r}(n).
 \label{crit:eq-hankel-smallness}
\end{align}
Therefore the universally cleared nonzero integer $Q_n(s)\mathcal D_n(s,r)$ grows at rate
$\frac12n^3\log s+O(n^2)$: this cyclotomic integerizer costs four times the cubic decay.
When $r=s^k$, the determinant vanishes for $n>k$, recovering integral-exponent finite rank;
off that locus its signs depend only on $\lfloor\log_s r\rfloor$.  The detector is exact but
this universal clearing has no subunit arithmetic regime.  Specialization-dependent gcd
cancellation can reduce the actual denominator and is not controlled by this calculation,
so the statement is deliberately not a reduced-denominator lower bound.

There is an independent fixed-support obstruction.  If $a,b>1$ are multiplicatively
independent integers, the reduced denominator $B_n$ of
$(b^n-1)/(a^n-1)$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \log B_n=n\log a-o(n).
 \label{crit:eq-bcz-denominator}
\end{equation}
Indeed, the Bugeaud--Corvaja--Zannier gcd theorem~\cite{BCZ2003} makes the cancelled part subexponential,
whereas LTE makes the part supported on any fixed finite prime set only polynomial in $n$.
Consequently the quotient lies outside every fixed $S$-integer ring for all sufficiently
large $n$---there is not even an unbounded fixed-$S$ subsequence.  At a prime index $n$,
every surviving denominator prime outside the fixed divisors of $a-1$ has exact
multiplicative order $n$.  Since the fixed part is only polynomial and the full denominator
is exponential, fresh order-$n$ primes occur for every sufficiently large prime $n$, and are
distinct for distinct indices.  Hence the literal Hadamard-quotient strategy requires a
hypothesis that a conditional counterexample provably violates.

\subsection{Pure denominators still miss the Subspace threshold}
\label{crit:ridout}

Write a hypothetical nonintegral exponent as $x=B+\eta$, where $B\in\Nzero$ and
$0<\eta<1$, and in lowest terms write
\[
 2^\eta=\frac{W}{2^a},\qquad 3^\eta=\frac{Z}{3^b},
 \qquad 2\nmid W,\quad 3\nmid Z.
\]
For a convergent $p/q$ to $\eta$, put
\[
 \varepsilon=q\eta-p,\qquad K=aq+p,\qquad L=bq+p.
\]
For every sufficiently large convergent, $p,K,L\ge1$; all statements below are restricted to
that tail.  Set
\[
 X=\frac{W^q}{2^K}=2^\varepsilon,\qquad
 Y=\frac{Z^q}{3^L}=3^\varepsilon.
\]
The strongest joint pure-support fraction is already reduced:
\begin{equation}
 X-Y=\frac{C_{p,q}}{D_{p,q}},\qquad
 C_{p,q}=W^q3^L-Z^q2^K,\qquad D_{p,q}=2^K3^L,\qquad
 \gcd(C_{p,q},6)=1.
 \label{crit:eq-pure-cross}
\end{equation}
The parity and mod-$3$ assertions prove the gcd statement, while
\begin{equation}
 D_{p,q}=(WZ)^q6^{-\varepsilon},\qquad
 C_{p,q}=D_{p,q}(2^\varepsilon-3^\varepsilon).
 \label{crit:eq-pure-height}
\end{equation}
A two-logarithm Baker lower bound~\cite{Baker1975} and the convergent upper bound give constants
$c_1,c_2,\kappa>0$ such that
\begin{equation}
 c_1D_{p,q}q^{-\kappa}\le |C_{p,q}|\le c_2D_{p,q}q^{-1}.
 \label{crit:eq-pure-barrier}
\end{equation}
Thus $|C_{p,q}|=D_{p,q}^{1-o(1)}$.  Ridout's theorem or Schmidt's Subspace
theorem~\cite{Ridout1958,Schmidt1980} would require a
fixed saving $D_{p,q}^{1-\rho}$ with $\rho>0$; Baker proves that no such inequality can
hold eventually.  For every fixed nonzero $P\in\Q[X,Y]$, contact rigidity gives
\[
 \operatorname{ord}_{t=0}P(2^t,3^t)
 \le \deg_XP+\deg_YP.
\]
Indeed, the first nonzero homogeneous part of $P$ at $(1,1)$ evaluates at
$(\log2,\log3)$; any further cancellation would make the transcendental ratio
$\log_2 3$ algebraic.
Thus fixed-degree contact supplies only a polynomial-in-$q$ saving against the natural
exponential common-denominator scale.  This does not rule out $q$-dependent polynomials of
controlled height; a uniform theorem for such a family would be genuinely new.  The coprime
$2/3$ supports are exact, but the unrestricted primes of $C_{p,q}$ absorb the product formula.

\begin{statusbox}{This critical interpolation and closure layer contains several bounded
formal cores and exact paper-level advances.  The universal Lambert identity is \statuslean{} in
\lean{LambertCocycleFinite}; because it holds for arbitrary rational $M,N$, it is a certified
no-go.  The finite positivity/covariance core, Newton append/collision algebra, and higher
Newton--Kummer integral-exponent calibration are \statuslean{} in
\lean{PositiveCoefficientClosure}, \lean{NewtonCollisionCore}, and
\lean{RankOneNewtonKummer}.  Finite dilation-tail preservation and signed-orbit augmentation
are \statuslean{} in \lean{FiniteDilationAlternation} and \lean{SignedOrbitNormFinite}.
Private dyadic order, cleaned-gap capture, and adjacent-smooth
tangent algebra are \statuslean{} in \lean{DyadicPrivateSupport},
\lean{CaptureMultiplier}, and \lean{CatalanTangentCore}.  Their infinite-series, valuation,
asymptotic, Kummer-field, density, and resultant extensions remain explicitly
\statusnew{} paper arguments.  Together with the refined Stieltjes/Jensen, Hermite,
reciprocal-Hankel, BCZ, and pure-denominator results, they leave three narrower interfaces:
a positive arithmetic interpolant lying in a rigid cone such as nonnegative coefficients or
one-signed geometric curvature; an output-specific denominator upper bound on a balanced
exhaustion, or a saturated two-generator divisor of the positive Markov--Pad\'e defect integer, rather
than more fresh divisors; or exceptional
cross-conjugate ideal overlap that makes a signed Kummer operation integral.  The natural
Stieltjes transfer family, unsaturated Markov--Pad\'e Hankel Smith content, finite positive-dilation filters, finite and one-ray infinite
power-substitution corrections, four-dilation rank-one defect, sparse-spike aggregation,
pairwise triangular gap synchronization, and collision-tree/Smith control without
an output-sensitive estimate for the transverse bad-cluster factor and its $p$-adic lifts,
reciprocal Hankel determinants, ordinary traces, character projections, common ideals,
signed augmentation-zero ratios absent exceptional overlap, and subgroup output partial
norms do not improve the relevant bounds at their exact scales.  Fixed-level order-one
defining polynomials also supply no factor descent in the shift or Newton order.  None of the surviving
bridges is supplied by the original hypotheses.}
\end{statusbox}

\section{Prime-top cyclotomic isolation and growing linear stencils}
\label{sec:primetop}

Section~\ref{sec:orbit-height-entropy} showed that a \emph{fixed} Richardson order or fixed rational
contact cannot repair the exponential height loss of the rational symmetric secants
$J_k(r,s)=(s^k-s^{-k})/(r^k-r^{-k})$.  This section removes the word ``fixed.''  For a
hypothetical counterexample the level-$\ell$ secant at a prime $\ell$ carries, in its
\emph{reduced} denominator, almost the entire homogeneous cyclotomic factor
$\widehat\Phi_{2\ell}(P,Q)=(P^\ell+Q^\ell)/(P+Q)$, and no linear combination of lower levels
with coefficients of small prime support can cancel it.  Against a denominator of logarithmic
size $(\ell-1)\log P$ the real contact of an $m$-node maximally flat stencil supplies only
$2m\log(1/|h|)$, and Baker's bound makes $\log(1/|h|)=O(\log\log P)$ along convergents.  The
approximation exponent of every prime-top maximal-contact integer stencil therefore tends to
zero even when the order grows almost as fast as $1/|h|$.  The finite algebra is
\statuslean{} in \lean{PrimeTopIsolation}; the uniform gcd input and the nearest-pole
asymptotics are \statusnew{} with a \statusknown{} citation.

\subsection{Orbit-uniform generalized gcd}
\label{primetop:uniform-gcd}

Let $x\notin\Z$ with $M=2^x,A=3^x\in\Z$.  For $w=(a,b)\in\Z^2\setminus\{0\}$ put
$r_w=2^a3^b$ and $s_w=M^aA^b=r_w^{\,x}$, oriented so that $r_w>1$, and write
$r_w=P/Q$, $s_w=U/V$ in lowest terms.  The decisive observation is that every pair
$(r_w^{\,n},s_w^{\,n})$ lies in the \emph{one} finitely generated group
\begin{equation}
 \Gamma_x=\langle(2,M),(3,A)\rangle\subset\mathbb G_m^2(\Q),
 \label{primetop:eq-fixed-group}
\end{equation}
and $r_w,s_w$ are multiplicatively independent for every $w\ne0$ (a relation
$r_w^cs_w^d=1$ gives $c+dx=0$, hence $x\in\Q$ and then $x\in\Z$).  Corvaja--Zannier's
theorem for a fixed finitely generated subgroup of $\mathbb G_m^2$ \cite{CorvajaZannier2005}
has a finite exceptional set, which cannot follow an unbounded sequence of changing
directions.  Hence, uniformly in $w$,
\begin{equation}
 \log\gcd(P^n-Q^n,U^n-V^n)=o_x(n\log P)\qquad(n\log P\to\infty).
 \label{primetop:eq-uniform-gcd}
\end{equation}
The orbit-height calculation of Section~\ref{sec:orbit-height-entropy} used the same theorem along
one ray; \eqref{primetop:eq-uniform-gcd} is the moving-direction form.

\subsection{Order of every fresh prime}
\label{primetop:fresh-order}

For an odd prime $\ell$ define
$\widehat\Phi_{2\ell}(P,Q)=\sum_{i<\ell}P^i(-Q)^{\ell-1-i}$, so that
$(P+Q)\widehat\Phi_{2\ell}(P,Q)=P^\ell+Q^\ell$ and
$\log\widehat\Phi_{2\ell}(P,Q)=(\ell-1)\log P+O(1)$.

\begin{lemma}[Fresh primes]\label{primetop:lem-fresh}
Let $\ell$ be an odd prime, $P,Q$ coprime integers, and $p\ne\ell$ a prime dividing
$\widehat\Phi_{2\ell}(P,Q)$.  Then $p\nmid PQ(P+Q)$, the residue $PQ^{-1}$ has exact order
$2\ell$ in $\mathbb F_p^\times$, $2\ell\mid p-1$, and $p\nmid P^{2k}-Q^{2k}$ for
$0<k<\ell$.  Moreover $v_\ell(\widehat\Phi_{2\ell}(P,Q))\le1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Coprimality excludes $p\mid P$ or $p\mid Q$ from $p\mid P^\ell+Q^\ell$.  If $p\mid P+Q$ then
$Q\equiv-P$ and $\widehat\Phi_{2\ell}\equiv\ell P^{\ell-1}\pmod p$, forcing $p=\ell$.  Thus
$y=PQ^{-1}$ satisfies $y^\ell=-1\ne1$ (here $p\ne2$ because $P^\ell+Q^\ell$ is odd) and
$y^2\ne1$ (as $y\ne\pm1$), so $\operatorname{ord}(y)=2\ell$ and $2\ell\mid p-1$.  If
$p\mid P^{2k}-Q^{2k}$ then $2\ell\mid2k$, impossible for $0<k<\ell$.  The $\ell$-adic bound
is lifting-the-exponent.
\end{proof}

All parts except the last are \statuslean{} in \lean{PrimeTopIsolation} (the order,
the divisibility $2\ell\mid p-1$, and the lower-level integrality are separate theorems).  Define
the \emph{fresh factor}
\begin{equation}
 \mathfrak F_\ell=\Bigl(\frac{\widehat\Phi_{2\ell}(P,Q)}
 {\gcd(\widehat\Phi_{2\ell}(P,Q),U^{2\ell}-V^{2\ell})}\Bigr)_{(\ell)},
 \label{primetop:eq-fresh-factor}
\end{equation}
the prime-to-$\ell$ part after removing target-gap cancellation.  By
\eqref{primetop:eq-uniform-gcd} and the lemma,
\begin{equation}
 \log\mathfrak F_\ell=(\ell-1)\log P-o_x(\ell\log P)
 \qquad(\ell\log P\to\infty\text{ through odd primes}),
 \label{primetop:eq-fresh-mass}
\end{equation}
uniformly over varying directions.

\subsection{Reduced-denominator survival and the coefficient tax}
\label{primetop:survival}

Let $p^d\parallel\mathfrak F_\ell$ with $\ell$ larger than every prime divisor of $MA$.
Since $p>2\ell$ and $p\nmid PQ\,UV$, Lemma~\ref{primetop:lem-fresh} gives
$v_p(J_\ell)=-d$ and $v_p(J_k)\ge0$ for $1\le k<\ell$.  The ultrametric unique-minimum
lemma (\statuslean{}, \lean{padicValRat_sum_eq_top}) then yields:

\begin{theorem}[Stencil survival]\label{primetop:thm-survival}
If $a_1,\dots,a_\ell\in\Q$ with $a_\ell\ne0$ satisfy $v_p(a_\ell)=0$ and $v_p(a_k)\ge0$
at every prime $p\mid\mathfrak F_\ell$, then
$\mathfrak F_\ell\mid\operatorname{den}\bigl(\sum_{k\le\ell}a_kJ_k\bigr)$, and hence
$\log\operatorname{den}\ge(\ell-1)\log P-o_x(\ell\log P)$.
\end{theorem}

Without any support hypothesis there is still a local tax.  Put
$C_p=\max_{a_k\ne0}|v_p(a_k)|$ and $E_p=\max(0,-v_p(S))$ for $S=\sum a_kJ_k$.

\begin{proposition}[Coefficient-or-denominator tax]\label{primetop:prop-tax}
$2(E_p+C_p)\ge d$ for every $p^d\parallel\mathfrak F_\ell$.  Consequently
$\log\operatorname{den}(S)+2\sum_kh(a_k)\ge\tfrac12\log\mathfrak F_\ell$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
If $2C_p\ge d$ there is nothing to prove.  Otherwise the top summand has valuation
$v_p(a_\ell)-d<-d/2$ while every other nonzero summand has valuation $\ge-C_p>-d/2$, so the
unique-minimum lemma gives $v_p(S)=v_p(a_\ell)-d$ and $E_p\ge d-C_p$.
\end{proof}

The local inequality is \statuslean{} (\lean{coefficient_tax}); the height form uses
$\sum_p|v_p(a)|\log p\le2h(a)$.  The factor $\tfrac12$ is sharp for this dichotomy.  The
conclusion is not that adaptive coefficients are impossible, but that a proposed cancellation
must visibly carry the moving prime mass it removes.

\subsection{Maximal-contact stencils and nearest-pole asymptotics}
\label{primetop:stencils}

Let $f_x(z)=\sinh(xz)/\sinh z$ and let $1\le n_1<\dots<n_m=N$ be integer nodes with
$\lambda_i=n_i^2$.  The weights $w_i=\prod_{j\ne i}\lambda_j/(\lambda_j-\lambda_i)$ are the
Lagrange weights reproducing the value at $0$ for polynomials in $z^2$ of degree $<m$, and
$\mathcal S_{\mathbf n,x}(e^h)=\sum_iw_if_x(n_ih)=\sum_iw_iJ_{n_i}(r,s)$ is rational for a
$2$--$3$ rational $r=e^h$.  The moments satisfy $M_0=1$, $M_j=0$ for $0<j<m$, and
$M_m=(-1)^{m-1}\prod\lambda_i$, with generating identity
$\sum_{j}(M_j-\mathbf 1_{j=0})t^j=(-1)^{m-1}(\prod_i\lambda_i)t^m/\prod_i(1-\lambda_it)$.
Every prime in a weight $w_i$ is below $2N$ (only $n_j$, $n_j\pm n_i$ occur), so for prime
$N=\ell$ larger than the prime support of $MA$, Theorem~\ref{primetop:thm-survival}
applies with zero coefficients at unused levels:
\begin{equation}
 \mathfrak F_N\mid\operatorname{den}\mathcal S_{\mathbf n,x}(e^h),\qquad
 \log\operatorname{den}\mathcal S_{\mathbf n,x}(e^h)\ge(N-1)\log P-o_x(N\log P).
 \label{primetop:eq-stencil-den}
\end{equation}
For consecutive nodes the weights are $c_{m,k}=2(-1)^{k-1}\binom{2m}{m+k}/\binom{2m}{m}$ and
the stencil is a central difference:
$\mathcal R_{m,x}(e^h)-x=(-1)^{m+1}\binom{2m}{m}^{-1}\delta_h^{2m}f_x(0)$, equivalently
$\sum_{k\le m}c_{m,k}\cosh(kt)=1-(-1)^m\binom{2m}{m}^{-1}(2\sinh(t/2))^{2m}$.  On integer
exponents this gives the exact finite sums
$\mathcal R_{m,L}(e^h)-L=-2(-1)^m\binom{2m}{m}^{-1}\sum_j(2\sinh(jh))^{2m}$ over
$j\le(L-1)/2$ (odd $L$; half-integer shifts for even $L$), which separate the integral locus
from the pole-dominated regime below.

For $x\notin\Z$ the nearest poles of $f_x$ are $\pm i\pi$, with principal part
$2\pi\sin(\pi x)/(z^2+\pi^2)$; Cauchy estimates on $|z|\le\rho<2\pi$ give
$b_j(x)=2(-1)^j\sin(\pi x)\pi^{-2j-1}+O(\rho^{-2j})$ for the Taylor coefficients of $f_x$.
Inserting this into the exact tail
$\mathcal S-x=(-1)^{m-1}(\prod\lambda_i)h^{2m}\sum_{r}b_{m+r}h^{2r}h_r(\lambda)$ (complete
homogeneous $h_r$) and summing the geometric series gives, whenever $m\to\infty$ and
$N|h|\to0$,
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal S_{\mathbf n,x}(e^h)-x
 =-\frac{2\sin\pi x}{\pi}\prod_{i=1}^m\frac{n_i^2h^2}{\pi^2+n_i^2h^2}\,(1+o_x(1)),
 \label{primetop:eq-pole-product}
\end{equation}
eventually nonzero with the fixed sign $-\operatorname{sgn}\sin\pi x$; the remainder is
exponentially small in $m$ because $h^2\sum n_i^2\le mN^2h^2=o(m)$.

\subsection{The growing-order no-go}
\label{primetop:nogo}

Let $p_j/q_j$ be convergents to $\log3/\log2$, $h_j=q_j\log3-p_j\log2$, oriented with
$r_j=e^{|h_j|}=P_j/Q_j>1$, so $\log P_j\asymp q_j$ and $|h_j|\ll q_j^{-1}$.  A lower bound
for linear forms in two logarithms \cite{BakerWustholz1993,LaurentMignotteNesterenko} gives
$|h_j|\ge C_0q_j^{-C_1}$, hence $\log(1/|h_j|)=O(\log q_j)=o(\log P_j)$.

\begin{theorem}[Prime-top maximal-contact stencils are weak]\label{primetop:thm-nogo}
Let $N_j$ be odd primes with $N_j|h_j|\to0$, and let $S_j$ be any maximal-contact integer
stencil with $m_j\to\infty$ nodes and largest node $N_j$ evaluated at $e^{|h_j|}$.  Then
\[
 \frac{-\log|S_j-x|}{\log\operatorname{den}(S_j)}\longrightarrow0,
\]
so $|S_j-x|>\operatorname{den}(S_j)^{-\eta}$ for every fixed $\eta>0$ and all large $j$.
In particular this holds for Richardson orders $\ell_j\asymp q_j^{1/2}$ (Bertrand).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By \eqref{primetop:eq-stencil-den}, $\log\operatorname{den}(S_j)\ge(1-o(1))N_j\log P_j$.
By \eqref{primetop:eq-pole-product},
$-\log|S_j-x|\le2m_j\log(C/|h_j|)+o(m_j)\le2N_j\log(C/|h_j|)+o(N_j)$.  Divide and use
$\log(1/|h_j|)=o(\log P_j)$.
\end{proof}

Prime-top isolation contributes denominator mass $\asymp N\log P$ while real contact supplies
at most $m\log(1/|h|)$ with $m\le N$; the ratio is $O(\log q/q)$ no matter how the nodes move.
The theorem does not cover nonlinear constructions, stencils whose largest index leaves the
near-identity window $N|h|\to0$, or coefficient systems not chosen by maximal polynomial
contact; those remain genuine options, and Proposition~\ref{primetop:prop-tax} is the first
test any of them must pass.

\subsection{Covolume conservation for restricted denominators}
\label{primetop:covolume}

A separate proposal forces approximation denominators to carry prescribed $p$-adic depth and
then combines real and $p$-adic smallness.  For $L=\prod_{p\in S}p^{e_p}$ the lattice
$\{(q,q\beta-a):q\in L\Z,\,a\in\Z\}$ has covolume $L$, so Minkowski---or, more simply,
Dirichlet's pigeonhole applied to $L\beta$---supplies $0<q\le nL$ with $L\mid q$ and
$|q\beta-a|\le1/(n+1)\le L/q$, while every such $q$ has $\prod_{p\in S}|q|_p\le L^{-1}$.
Therefore
\begin{equation}
 |q\beta-a|\prod_{p\in S}|q|_p\le\frac1q,
 \label{primetop:eq-covolume}
\end{equation}
exactly the unrestricted Dirichlet exponent; and for each fixed $L$ a badly approximable
$\beta=\alpha/L$ shows $|q\beta-a|\ge cL/q$ on $L\Z$, so the scale $L/Q$ is sharp.  The
one-prime statement is \statuslean{} (\lean{covolume_conservation} in
\lean{RestrictedDenominatorDirichlet}); the several-prime version is the product of local
factors.  The law rules out only the direct strategy ``impose $q\equiv0\pmod L$ and invoke
Minkowski''; accidental extra divisibility, correlations with the numerator, or
output-specific congruences are outside its scope.

\subsection{What remains viable}
\label{primetop:remaining}

The results narrow the search to three interfaces: a \emph{nonlinear} construction that
escapes prime-top isolation (any proposal should first be run through
Lemma~\ref{primetop:lem-fresh} and Proposition~\ref{primetop:prop-tax}); an
\emph{output-specific} local-to-global cancellation involving several correlated cyclotomic
factors rather than one pair (the orbit-uniform bound shows that direct cancellation between
$\widehat\Phi_{2\ell}(P,Q)$ and $U^{2\ell}-V^{2\ell}$ has only $o(\ell\log P)$ mass); or a
\emph{tensor-period} statement controlling the quadratic relation
$\log M\log3-\log A\log2=0$.  Logarithms of algebraic numbers are periods of Kummer
$1$-motives, for which the period conjecture is known through the analytic subgroup theorem,
but the quadratic relation lives in a tensor square outside that linear theory; the
function-field analogue (algebraic independence for Drinfeld-module logarithms via Frobenius
difference equations) illustrates the missing operator-level symmetry but is not applicable
here.  A concrete intermediate problem: for every rational expression of bounded degree in
the prime-top values $J_1,\dots,J_\ell$, either a positive proportion of
$\log\widehat\Phi_{2\ell}(P,Q)$ survives in its reduced height or the expression factors
through an explicit multiplicative dependence.

\section{The sparse quadratic prime-logarithm class}
\label{sec:sparsequad}

The log-product criterion of Section~\ref{sec:logproduct} and the formal prime determinant
of Section~\ref{crit:support-defects} treat the relation
$\log m\log3-\log n\log2=0$ as a linear form in products of prime logarithms.  This section
records the exact \emph{local} structure of that form at an external prime, a $q$-adic
realization that is unconditionally nonzero, the narrowest period-stability principle that
would close the problem, and---new here---the calibration that this principle is
\emph{equivalent} to the conjecture.  The canonical-generator, counting, and
commensurability statements that accompany this viewpoint are already in
Sections~\ref{sec:conditional} and~\ref{cd:counting} and are not repeated.

\subsection{The formal class and its external derivatives}
\label{sparsequad:class}

Introduce formal variables $L_p$ ($p$ prime), $L(u)=\sum_pv_p(u)L_p$, and
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal F_{m,n}=L(m)L_3-L(n)L_2,
 \qquad\operatorname{ev}_\infty(L_p)=\log p.
 \label{sparsequad:eq-class}
\end{equation}
A candidate has $\operatorname{ev}_\infty(\mathcal F_{m,n})=0$, and
$\mathcal F_{m,n}=0$ formally iff $m=2^k,n=3^k$ (compare the monomials $L_qL_3$, $L_qL_2$,
$L_3^2$, $L_2^2$, $L_2L_3$).  For an external prime $q\notin\{2,3\}$,
\begin{equation}
 \partial_q\mathcal F_{m,n}=a_qL_3-b_qL_2,\qquad
 \Lambda_q:=\operatorname{ev}_\infty(\partial_q\mathcal F_{m,n})
 =\log\frac{3^{a_q}}{2^{b_q}},
 \label{sparsequad:eq-derivative}
\end{equation}
with $a_q=v_q(m)$, $b_q=v_q(n)$.  By Section~\ref{sec:smooth} every nonintegral candidate
has an external prime in the support of $mn$, and for such $q$ unique factorization gives
$\Lambda_q\ne0$, quantitatively
\begin{equation}
 |\Lambda_q|\ge\frac1{\max(3^{a_q},2^{b_q})}
 \label{sparsequad:eq-elementary-lower}
\end{equation}
(from $|\log(A/B)|\ge|A-B|/\max(A,B)$).  Both facts are \statuslean{}
(\lean{external_derivative_ne_zero}, \lean{abs_external_derivative_ge} in
\lean{SparseCoaction}).  Thus the hypothetical zero of $\mathcal F_{m,n}$ at the
prime-logarithm point is \emph{nonsingular}: its gradient is nonzero.  Methods that detect
only factorized or singular period relations cannot reach the conjecture.  The derivatives
at the structural primes are $\partial_2\mathcal F=a_2L_3-b_2L_2-L(n)$ and
$\partial_3\mathcal F=a_3L_3+L(m)-b_3L_2$, whose evaluations still involve $x$; only the
external derivatives eliminate $x$ and become logarithms of explicit rationals.  Euler's
identity $2\mathcal F=\sum_qL_q\partial_q\mathcal F$ exhibits the zero period as a weighted
cancellation among first derivatives of which at least one is unconditionally nonzero.

Writing $r_{\mathrm{ext}}=\operatorname{rank}\{(a_q,b_q):q\notin\{2,3\}\}\in\{1,2\}$, the
rank-one case has $(a_q,b_q)=c_q(A,B)$ with coprime $(A,B)$, so $m=2^{a_2}3^{a_3}U^A$,
$n=2^{b_2}3^{b_3}U^B$ with $U=\prod q^{c_q}$ and the relation collapses to the
three-logarithm form
\[
 a_3(\log3)^2-b_2(\log2)^2+(a_2-b_3)\log2\log3+\log U\,(A\log3-B\log2)=0;
\]
in rank two, two external primes give independent descendants.  This refines the external
rank classification of Section~\ref{sec:valuationlattice}.  As a symmetric operator on the
prime-indexed vector space the form has rank at most four (image in
$\operatorname{span}\{[m],[n],e_2,e_3\}$), independently of the number of prime divisors of
$mn$: the prime-logarithm vector would be an isotropic, non-radical point of an ``arrowhead''
form of rank $\le4$.

\subsection{A nonarchimedean realization}
\label{sparsequad:qadic}

For $q\ge5$ let $\log_q$ be the Iwasawa logarithm on $\Q_q^\times$ ($\log_q q=0$).  On
positive rationals its kernel is $q^\Z$ (the only positive rational root of unity is $1$).
Define $\rho_q([u]\odot[v])=v_q(u)\log_q v+v_q(v)\log_q u$ on symmetric products of exponent
vectors; then $\rho_q(\mathcal F_{m,n})=\log_q(3^{a_q}/2^{b_q})$, which is nonzero because
$3^{a_q}/2^{b_q}$ is a $q$-unit different from $1$.  A candidate would therefore have the
profile $\operatorname{ev}_\infty(\mathcal F_{m,n})=0$, $\rho_q(\mathcal F_{m,n})\ne0$.  The
first nonzero $q$-adic digit is detected by a finite congruence: with
$R=3^{a_q}/2^{b_q}$ and $h_q(R)=v_q(R^{q-1}-1)\ge1$ one has $v_q(\log_qR)=h_q(R)$, so
$R^{q-1}\not\equiv1\pmod{q^{h_q(R)+1}}$; for $h_q=1$ this is the ordinary Fermat quotient
(compare \lean{FermatQuotientDeterminant}).  No comparison theorem currently turns the
archimedean/$q$-adic mismatch into a contradiction.

\subsection{Sparse coaction separation is the conjecture}
\label{sparsequad:scs}

In the mixed-Tate category over $\Z[1/6mn]$ the decomposable weight-two class
$\mathcal K_{m,n}=\ell^{\mathfrak m}(m)\ell^{\mathfrak m}(3)-\ell^{\mathfrak m}(n)\ell^{\mathfrak m}(2)$
has real period $\log m\log3-\log n\log2$, and the prime-valuation functional applied to the
de Rham factor of its $(1,1)$ coaction component gives
$D_q\mathcal K_{m,n}=\ell^{\mathfrak m}(3^{a_q}/2^{b_q})$ with real period $\Lambda_q\ne0$.
So a candidate gives a \emph{nonzero} motivic class with zero period and an explicit nonzero
first descendant.  The narrowest principle that would finish is:

\begin{definition}[Sparse coaction separation]\label{sparsequad:def-scs}
For all positive integers $u,v$ with $\log u\log3=\log v\log2$ and every prime
$q\notin\{2,3\}$: $v_q(u)\log3=v_q(v)\log2$.
\end{definition}

One must not infer $\operatorname{ev}_\infty(\partial_qF)=0$ from
$\operatorname{ev}_\infty(F)=0$ for an arbitrary numerical relation; evaluation kernels are
not stable under formal differentiation.  The coaction argument is valid only once a
numerical relation is known to come from a motivic relation, which is exactly the missing
injectivity.

\begin{theorem}[Calibration]\label{sparsequad:thm-scs}
Sparse coaction separation is \emph{equivalent} to Conjecture~\ref{conj:AE}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
($\Rightarrow$) Given a nonintegral candidate, pick an external support prime $q$; the
principle forces $\Lambda_q=0$, contradicting \eqref{sparsequad:eq-elementary-lower}.
($\Leftarrow$) Given $u,v>0$ with $\log u\log3=\log v\log2$, put $t=\log u/\log2$; then
$2^t=u$ and $3^t=e^{t\log3}=e^{\log v}=v$ are integers, so the conjecture gives $t\in\Z$,
$t\ge0$, hence $u=2^t$, $v=3^t$ and $v_q(u)=v_q(v)=0$ for every external $q$.
\end{proof}

Both directions are \statuslean{} in \lean{SparseCoaction}, as the single equivalence
\lean{sparseCoactionSeparation_iff_alaogluErdosConjecture}.
The calibration matters: the principle was proposed as a ``deliberately narrow target,'' but
its surplus generality---arbitrary $u,v$ rather than outputs of a single exponent---is
illusory, exactly as for the prime-log-product criterion in Section~\ref{lp:criterion-remarks}.  A
proof of separation for decomposable weight-two Kummer classes with one fixed factor in
$\{\ell2,\ell3\}$ would be a proof of the conjecture, not a reduction of it; conversely,
nothing short of the conjecture proves the separation.  The useful content is the precise
\emph{witness}: the required injectivity has a fully explicit, minimal-weight descendant,
and any argument using only the numerical equality of products of logarithms, without a
mechanism making the relation coaction-stable, silently assumes the conclusion.

\subsection{Convergent gaps under \texorpdfstring{$abc$}{abc}}
\label{sparsequad:abc}

Write $m=2^aM_0$ with $M_0$ odd and $n=3^bN_0$ with $3\nmid N_0$; for a nonintegral
candidate neither $M_0$ nor $N_0$ is $1$.  Let $p_j/q_j$ be convergents of
$y=\log M_0/\log2$ and $G_j=M_0^{q_j}-2^{p_j}$; then $\gcd(G_j,2M_0)=1$.  Similarly
$H_j=N_0^{s_j}-3^{r_j}$ from convergents of $\log N_0/\log3$.

\begin{proposition}[Radical-full gaps]\label{sparsequad:prop-abc}
Assume the $abc$ conjecture.  Then
$\log\operatorname{rad}|G_j|/\log|G_j|\to1$ and likewise for $H_j$; equivalently
$|G_j|/\operatorname{rad}|G_j|=|G_j|^{o(1)}$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The three numbers $\min(M_0^{q_j},2^{p_j})$, $|G_j|$, $\max(\cdot)$ are pairwise coprime,
so $abc$ gives $\max(M_0^{q_j},2^{p_j})\le K_\varepsilon\operatorname{rad}(2M_0G_j)^{1+\varepsilon}$,
hence $\operatorname{rad}|G_j|\ge c_\varepsilon\max(\cdot)^{1/(1+\varepsilon)}$ while
$\log|G_j|\le q_j\log M_0+o(q_j)=\log\max(\cdot)+o(q_j)$.  Let $\varepsilon\downarrow0$.
\end{proof}

No lower bound for the continued-fraction error is used.  The consequence for Frey-type
curves $Y^2=X(X-M_0^{q_j})(X-2^{p_j})$ is that the repeated powers in the two main terms do
\emph{not} produce a bounded or slowly growing level: the gap injects exponentially many
distinct primes into the discriminant.  Baker-type bounds control the \emph{size} of the gap
(finite irrationality measure of $y$); $abc$ controls its \emph{radical}.  The two are
complementary, and a modular strategy must supply an independent reason for the gap primes
to disappear from the residual conductor.

\section{Mesoscopic factorial cocycles}
\label{sec:factorialcocycle}

This section develops an auxiliary construction not treated elsewhere in the report: signed
products of the falling factorials $F_n=(A^n)_{M^n}=A^n!/(A^n-M^n)!$.  Its archimedean side
is exactly solvable, its arithmetic side is exactly hostile, and the two determine a precise
linear-width escape target.  The elementary identities are \statuslean{} in
\lean{FactorialCocycle}; the prime-window theorem is \statusnew{} with \statusknown{}
analytic inputs.

\subsection{The one-divergent-cumulant regime}
\label{fc:regime}

With $\alpha=\log M/\log A=\log2/\log3$, the inequalities $4>3$ and $8<9$ give
$\tfrac12<\alpha<\tfrac23$ (\statuslean{}).  Put $N_n=A^n$, $K_n=M^n=N_n^\alpha$, and
\begin{equation}
 q=\frac MA=\Bigl(\frac23\Bigr)^x,\qquad
 \lambda=\frac{M^2}{A}=\Bigl(\frac43\Bigr)^x>1,\qquad
 \eta=\frac{M^3}{A^2}=\Bigl(\frac89\Bigr)^x<1,\qquad
 \tau=\frac{M^4}{A^3}<q<\eta.
 \label{fc:eq-modes}
\end{equation}
For $K_n$ balls in $N_n$ boxes the pair-collision scale $K_n^2/N_n=\lambda^n$ diverges while
the triple-collision scale $K_n^3/N_n^2=\eta^n$ vanishes; no information about the size of
$x$ is needed.  The kernel bound $x\ge12$ (\lean{FiniteCheck4096}; now $x\ge13$ by
\lean{FiniteCheck8192}) enters only through $q\le(2/3)^{12}=0.0077\ldots$.

\subsection{Exact expansion and fixed-shift classification}
\label{fc:classification}

From $-\log(1-u)=u+u^2/2+O(u^3/(1-u))$ and the first two power sums,
\begin{equation}
 \log F_n=nM^n\log A-\tfrac12\lambda^n+\tfrac12q^n-\tfrac16\eta^n+O(\tau^n).
 \label{fc:eq-expansion}
\end{equation}
For $P(T)=\sum_jc_jT^j\in\Z[T]$ let $\mathcal F_{P,n}=\prod_jF_{n+j}^{c_j}$, so
$\log\mathcal F_{P,n}=P(E)(\log F)_n$ with $E$ the forward shift.  The shift identities
\begin{equation}
 P(E)(\rho^n)=P(\rho)\rho^n,\qquad
 P(E)(n\rho^n)=\rho^n\bigl(nP(\rho)+\rho P'(\rho)\bigr)
 \label{fc:eq-shift}
\end{equation}
(\statuslean{}, \lean{shiftEval_geom}, \lean{shiftEval_mul_geom}) give the master asymptotic
\[
 \log\mathcal F_{P,n}=\log A\,M^n\bigl(nP(M)+MP'(M)\bigr)-\tfrac12P(\lambda)\lambda^n
 +\tfrac12P(q)q^n-\tfrac16P(\eta)\eta^n+O_P(\tau^n).
\]

\begin{theorem}[Near-unit classification]\label{fc:thm-classification}
$\mathcal F_{P,n}\to1$ if and only if $P(M)=P'(M)=P(M^2/A)=0$, i.e.\ iff
$P_*\mid P$ in $\Z[T]$ where, with $g=\gcd(A,M^2)$,
\[
 P_*(T)=(T-M)^2\Bigl(\frac AgT-\frac{M^2}g\Bigr)
 =-\frac{M^4}g+\frac{M^2(A+2M)}gT-\frac{M^2+2AM}gT^2+\frac AgT^3 .
\]
The minimal cocycle satisfies $\log\mathcal F_{P_*,n}=C_*\eta^n+O(q^n)$ with
$C_*=\frac{M^2(A-M)}{6gA}\bigl(M-\frac{M^3}{A^2}\bigr)^2>0$, so
$\mathcal F_{P_*,n}>1$ for large $n$.  Every nonzero annihilator has at least three
coefficient sign variations (Descartes, three positive roots).
\end{theorem}

The three annihilations, the vanishing of all three growing modes under $P_*(E)$, and the
coefficient expansion are \statuslean{} in \lean{FactorialCocycle}; necessity uses the
separation $M>\lambda>1$ of the growing modes.  When $P(M)=P'(M)=0$ the visible powers
$(A^n)^{M^n}$ cancel exactly (their exponent is $M^n(nP(M)+MP'(M))=0$), so
$\prod_jR_{n+j}^{c_j}=\mathcal F_{P,n}$ for the no-collision probabilities
$R_n=F_n/(A^n)^{M^n}$: the obstruction is the primitive prime content of the terminal
intervals $(A^t-M^t,A^t]$ themselves.  Cancelling further collision modes
$\rho_{r,s}=M^s/A^r$ (only $r=1,s=2$ exceeds one; the subunit ladder begins
$\eta,q,\tau,(M/A)^2,\dots$) makes $|\mathcal F_{P,n}-1|$ smaller but never changes the
sign-variation count or the fixed degree, and the next mode after $\eta$ decays at the rate
$x\log(3/2)$ that also governs the thickness threshold below---a critical coincidence rather
than slack.

\subsection{The prime-window denominator theorem}
\label{fc:primewindow}

By Legendre, $V_p(t):=v_p(F_t)=\sum_{r\ge1}(\lfloor A^t/p^r\rfloor-\lfloor(A^t-M^t)/p^r\rfloor)$
counts multiples of $p^r$ in the terminal interval, and
$v_p(\mathcal F_{P,n})=\sum_jc_jV_p(n+j)$, $\log\operatorname{den}\mathcal F_{P,n}=\sum_p\max(0,-v_p)\log p$.
Two \statusknown{} inputs: Huxley's short-interval theorem
$\vartheta(X)-\vartheta(X-X^\gamma)\sim X^\gamma$ for $\gamma>7/12$ \cite{Huxley1972}
(our exponent is $\alpha=0.6309\ldots$), and Brun--Titchmarsh
$\pi(y+h)-\pi(y)\le2h/\log h$ \cite{MontgomeryVaughan2007}.

\begin{theorem}[Prime-window obstruction]\label{fc:thm-window}
Assume $x\ge12$ and fix $\varepsilon>0$.  Let $P_n\in\Z[T]$ be nonzero polynomials with a
negative coefficient, $k_n$ the highest negative index, and suppose the span satisfies
$d_n-k_n\le(\log_23-1-\varepsilon)(n+k_n)$.  Then
\[
 \log\operatorname{den}(\mathcal F_{P_n,n})\ge(-c_{n,k_n})(\Delta_\varepsilon+o(1))M^{n+k_n},
 \qquad
 \Delta_\varepsilon=1-\frac{8q}{(2-\log_23+\varepsilon(1-\alpha))(1-q)}>0 .
\]
In particular every fixed $P$ with a negative coefficient---hence every fixed near-unit---has
$\log\operatorname{den}\mathcal F_{P,n}\gg M^n$, while $|\mathcal F_{P_*,n}-1|\sim C_*\eta^n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
At level $N=n+k$ put $X=A^N$, $H=M^N$.  Each prime $p\in(X-H,X]$ occurs once in $F_N$ and in
no lower factor; it enters the denominator unless some higher positive factor $F_{N+\ell}$
captures a multiple $mp\in(Y_\ell-W_\ell,Y_\ell]$ with $Y_\ell=A^\ell X$, $W_\ell=M^\ell H$.
For fixed $m\asymp A^\ell$ this confines $p$ to an interval of length $\le2Hq^\ell$, and
there are at most $2+2A^\ell H/X$ multipliers.  The span hypothesis makes
$\log(2Hq^\ell)/\log X\ge2-\log_23+\varepsilon(1-\alpha)=:\delta_\varepsilon>0$, so
Brun--Titchmarsh bounds the logarithmic prime mass of each capture interval by
$(4/\delta_\varepsilon+o(1))Hq^\ell$; summing over multipliers and $\ell\le D$ gives covered
mass $\le(8q/(\delta_\varepsilon(1-q))+o(1))H$, the second geometric sum being negligible
because $q^NM^D\le e^{-\varepsilon N\log M}$.  For $x\ge12$ the coefficient is
$0.1497\ldots<1$ already at $\varepsilon=0$.  Huxley gives total mass $(1+o(1))H$, so
uncovered primes have mass $\ge(\Delta_\varepsilon+o(1))H$, and each contributes
$v_p\le c_{n,k}<0$.
\end{proof}

The same argument applies to binomial cocycles $\mathcal B_{P,n}=\prod_j\binom{A^{n+j}}{M^{n+j}}^{c_j}$,
whose near-unit classification adds a double root at $1$ (Stirling's $\tfrac12n\log M$
term): $P_{\mathrm{bin}}=(T-1)^2P_*$.  Two universal thresholds appear: the multiplier $m$
begins to drift at span $\ell/(n+k)\asymp1-\alpha=0.369\ldots$, but covering survives until
the higher interval is as long as the prime scale, at $\ell/(n+k)\asymp\log_23-1=0.585\ldots$.
For a fixed polynomial the obstruction is visible in one contiguous slice without the
$x\ge12$ input: with $\rho=\max\{(M/A)^{j-k}:j>k,c_j>0\}$, the primes in
$(X-(1-\epsilon)H,X-(\rho+\epsilon)H)$ occur in no positive factor, giving the sharper
$\log\operatorname{den}\ge(-c_k)(1-\rho+o(1))M^{n+k}$.

\subsection{The linear-width target and the structural-prime prefix}
\label{fc:target}

\begin{target}[Linear-width factorial feasibility]\label{fc:target-linear}
Decide whether there are $P_n\in\Z[T]$ with $P_n(M)=P_n'(M)=P_n(M^2/A)=0$,
$v_p(\mathcal F_{P_n,n})\ge0$ for all $p$, $\mathcal F_{P_n,n}\to1$, and
$\deg P_n-k_n\ge(\log_23-1-o(1))(n+k_n)$.  A positive answer with an eventual strict
inequality $\mathcal F_{P_n,n}\ne1$ (e.g.\ a sign-controlled first surviving mode) proves
the conjecture; a negative answer by a dual valuation certificate closes the family.
\emph{Update (session log): the constructive branch is empty ---
Corollary~\ref{log:cor-target-dead} shows conditions (2) and (3) already force $P_n=0$ for
any mesoscopic pair, so this target is resolved negatively; only integrality without
convergence to $1$ remains, and the LP computation of Section~\ref{log:lp-experiment}
indicates that it is empty too.  Final update: the residue is also gone --- the global
terminal-prime contraction (Theorem~\ref{cw:thm-contraction}) closes bare integrality for
every nonzero $P$ with $P(M)=0$, uniformly in degree and span; see
Section~\ref{sec:criticalwindow}.}
\end{target}

For fixed $(M,A,n,d)$ the conditions are three homogeneous linear equations plus the finite
system $\sum_jc_jV_p(n+j)\ge0$, $p\le A^{n+d}$, i.e.\ a rational polyhedral cone
$\mathcal C_{n,d}$ intersected with a codimension-three subspace; the proof above is a dual
certificate below the critical width, and the right search at the critical width is for
sparse dual certificates supported on prime windows and transported multiples (LP with exact
Farkas certificates, then ILP with $P_n=P_*S_n$, then prime-power constraints).

The factorial asymptotic uses only the ratio $\log2/\log3$ and cannot by itself distinguish a
hypothetical primitive pair from the controls $(2^m,3^m)$.  The first primitive-sensitive
ingredient is a structural prime $r\mid M$, $r\nmid A$ (or $s\mid A$, $s\nmid3$), which a
nonintegral solution must have.  For such $r$ with $r^{e}\parallel M$, the lowest $en$
base-$r$ digit positions create no carry when adding $M^n$ and $A^n-M^n$, so Kummer's theorem
gives
\begin{equation}
 v_r\binom{A^n}{M^n}\le\lfloor n\log_rA\rfloor-en
 \label{fc:eq-carry-free}
\end{equation}
(\statuslean{}, \lean{padicValNat_choose_le_of_pow_dvd}).  The high-prime obstruction has size
$M^n$; the structural valuation is $O(n)$.  A hybrid dual certificate combining the two
weightings (high primes constrain signs and span; a structural prime constrains the same
coefficients through long carry-free prefixes) is the first remaining direction that
genuinely uses nonintegrality rather than the ratio alone.

\section{Centered cyclotomic trace dynamics}
\label{sec:centeredtrace}

Every rational approximation $p/q$ to a hypothetical nonintegral $\beta$ produces the
\emph{synchronized} rational near-units
\begin{equation}
 z_2=\frac{M^q}{2^p}=2^{\delta},\qquad
 z_3=\frac{A^q}{3^p}=3^{\delta}=z_2^{\thetaq},\qquad\delta=q\beta-p,
 \label{ct:eq-germ}
\end{equation}
one small real parameter encoded by two rationals whose denominators are supported at the
structural primes.  The symmetric secants of Section~\ref{sec:orbit-height-entropy} put the unknown
exponent in the dilation slot; here the dilation is an auxiliary \emph{odd integer} $d$ and
the near-unit is the dynamical variable, so the maps can be iterated and every iterate
reduced prime by prime.  The finite core is \statuslean{} in \lean{CenteredTrace}.

\subsection{Traces, Bernoulli expansion, and exact defect}
\label{ct:traces}

For odd $d=2h+1$ define $T_d(z)=d^{-1}\sum_{j=-h}^hz^j=z^{-h}(z^d-1)/(d(z-1))$.  It is
reciprocal, $T_d(z)\ge1$ for $z>0$ with equality only at $z=1$ (AM--GM), and
$T_d(e^t)=\sinh(dt/2)/(d\sinh(t/2))$, with the Bernoulli--Jordan expansion
\begin{equation}
 \log T_d(e^t)=\sum_{r\ge1}\frac{B_{2r}(d^{2r}-1)}{2r(2r)!}t^{2r}
 =\frac{d^2-1}{24}t^2-\frac{d^4-1}{2880}t^4+\cdots,
 \label{ct:eq-bernoulli}
\end{equation}
obtained from $\log((e^u-1)/u)=u/2+\sum B_{2r}u^{2r}/(2r(2r)!)$; the linear terms cancel,
which is the analytic source of the quadratic contact.  Arithmetically,
$T_d(z)=d^{-1}\prod_{n\mid d,n>1}\mathcal C_n(z)$ with the centered factors
$\mathcal C_n=z^{-\varphi(n)/2}\Phi_n$, and
$\log\mathcal C_n(e^t)=\log\Phi_n(1)+\sum_rB_{2r}J_{2r}(n)t^{2r}/(2r(2r)!)$ with Jordan
totients $J_m$; summing $\sum_{n\mid d}J_m(n)=d^m$ recovers \eqref{ct:eq-bernoulli}.  (Raw
necklace coordinates have only first-order contact at $1$; centering by reciprocity removes
it.)

For coprime $a,b>0$ and $S_d(a,b)=(a^d-b^d)/(a-b)$,
\begin{equation}
 T_d(a/b)=\frac{S_d(a,b)}{d(ab)^h},\qquad
 \gcd(S_d(a,b),ab)=1,\qquad
 \gcd\bigl(S_d(a,b),d(ab)^h\bigr)=\gcd(S_d(a,b),d)\mid d,
 \label{ct:eq-exact-reduction}
\end{equation}
so reduction of one trace value cancels only a divisor of the fixed integer $d$.

\begin{theorem}[Exact defect factorization]\label{ct:thm-defect}
$S_{2h+1}(a,b)-(2h+1)(ab)^h=\sum_{j=1}^h(ab)^{h-j}(a^j-b^j)^2=(a-b)^2P_d(a,b)$ with
$P_d(a,b)=\sum_{j=1}^h(ab)^{h-j}\bigl((a^j-b^j)/(a-b)\bigr)^2>0$ symmetric of degree $d-3$;
$P_3=1$, $P_5=a^2+3ab+b^2$, $P_7=a^4+3a^3b+6a^2b^2+3ab^3+b^4$.  If $T_d(a/b)=a'/b'$ is reduced
and $u=a-b$, then $a'-b'=u^2P_d(a,b)/\gcd(S_d(a,b),d)$.
\end{theorem}

The sum-of-squares identity and the divisibility by $(a-b)^2$ are \statuslean{} in
\lean{CenteredTrace}, by induction on $h$.  Since
$S_d\ge d(ab)^h$, the reduced height satisfies $|h(T_d(z))-(d-1)h(z)|\le\log d$: local
contact is always two, arithmetic degree is $d-1$.  Hence for any composition
$\Psi=T_{d_m}\circ\dots\circ T_{d_1}$ the contact is $2^m$ while $\deg\Psi=\prod(d_i-1)\ge2^m$,
with equality exactly for pure cubic composition: the cubic trace is the unique
\emph{critical} member, every higher positive trace is subcritical before any cross-branch
cancellation.

\subsection{Exact cubic dynamics}
\label{ct:cubic}

$T_3(z)-1=(z-1)^2/(3z)$, an exact square.  For reduced $z_k=a_k/b_k$ and $u_k=a_k-b_k$,
\begin{equation}
 a_{k+1}=\frac{a_k^2+a_kb_k+b_k^2}{g_k},\quad b_{k+1}=\frac{3a_kb_k}{g_k},\quad
 u_{k+1}=\frac{u_k^2}{g_k},\quad g_k=3^{\mathbf 1_{3\mid u_k}},
 \label{ct:eq-cubic-recurrence}
\end{equation}
because $a^2+ab+b^2-3ab=(a-b)^2$, $\gcd(a^2+ab+b^2,ab)=1$, and
$3\mid a^2+ab+b^2\iff3\mid a-b$ (all \statuslean{}).  Therefore, for every prime
$\ell\ne3$, $v_\ell(u_k)=2^kv_\ell(u_0)$ exactly (\lean{padicValInt_sq_div_three}), and
$v_3(u_k)=1+2^k(v_3(u_0)-1)$ when $3\mid u_0$ (else $0$).  Two consequences:

\begin{corollary}[No new cross-orbit support]\label{ct:cor-no-new-support}
For two reduced cubic orbits with defects $u_k,v_k$:
$\operatorname{rad}_{\ne3}\gcd(u_k,v_k)=\operatorname{rad}_{\ne3}\gcd(u_0,v_0)$ and
$v_\ell(\gcd(u_k,v_k))=2^kv_\ell(\gcd(u_0,v_0))$ for $\ell\ne3$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proposition}[Critical saturation]\label{ct:prop-saturation}
For $z_0\in\Q_{>0}\setminus\{1\}$, $T_3^{\circ k}(z_0)\to1$ with
$\varepsilon_{k+1}=\varepsilon_k^2/(3(1+\varepsilon_k))$, while
$H_k^2/3\le H_{k+1}\le3H_k^2$, so the canonical height
$\widehat h_3(z_0)=\lim2^{-k}\log H_k$ exists, is positive, and differs from $\log H_0$ by at
most $\log3$; and $\varepsilon_k\ge1/b_k\ge1/H_k$.  Locally
$T_3^{\circ k}(e^t)-1=3^{1-2^k}t^{2^k}(1+\alpha_kt^2+O(t^4))$ with $\alpha_1=1/12$,
$\alpha_k=-2^{k-3}/3$ for $k\ge2$.
\end{proposition}

Applied to the synchronized germ, $R_{k;p,q}=E_{3,k}/E_{2,k}\in\Q_{>0}$ with
$E_{i,k}=T_3^{\circ k}(z_i)-1$ satisfies
$R_{k;p,q}=\thetaq^{2^k}\bigl(1+\alpha_k((\log3)^2-(\log2)^2)\delta^2+O_k(\delta^4)\bigr)$:
the contact $2^k$ of each branch does \emph{not} transfer to the ratio, whose relative error
stays quadratic in $\delta$, while its height is $O(2^kq)$.  By
Corollary~\ref{ct:cor-no-new-support}, any exceptional cancellation in $R_{k;p,q}$ is already
encoded in the initial gaps $M^q-2^p$ and $A^q-3^p$; iteration only raises their common
valuations to powers.  This closes, exactly rather than by a loose height estimate, every
``iterate until the rational number is too close to one'' argument based on the cubic trace.

\subsection{Prime traces and the two fifth-trace channels}
\label{ct:fifth}

For an odd prime $p\ge5$ one has $P_p(a,b)\equiv(a-b)^{p-3}\pmod p$ (Frobenius on
$S_p\equiv(a-b)^{p-1}$), $\gcd(S_p,p)=p$ iff $p\mid a-b$, and in that case
$v_p(P_p(a,b))=1$ exactly (evaluate on the diagonal: $P_p(b,b)=pb^{p-3}(p^2-1)/24$, and the
first derivative vanishes modulo $p$).  So the normalized factor
$C_p=P_p/p^{\mathbf 1_{p\mid a-b}}$ is a $p$-free integer and the reduced defect is
$a'-b'=(a-b)^2C_p(a,b)$: the fifth trace is the first level that can introduce new defect
primes, and the last whose new factor is a single rational reciprocal quadratic.

\begin{lemma}[Reciprocal-quadratic bridge]\label{ct:lem-bridge}
In any commutative ring, $cd(a^2+\lambda ab+b^2)-ab(c^2+\lambda cd+d^2)=(ad-bc)(ac-bd)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Two-channel decomposition]\label{ct:thm-channels}
Let $F(a,b)=a^2+3ab+b^2$, $(a,b)$ and $(c,d)$ coprime pairs, and $p\ne5$ a prime with
$p^e\mid F(a,b)$ and $p^e\mid F(c,d)$, $e\ge1$.  Then $p^e$ divides exactly one of the
channels $D_-=ad-bc$, $D_+=ac-bd$, and $p$ does not divide the other.  Consequently, with
$G=\gcd(C_1,C_2)$ of the normalized factors, $G=\gcd(G,D_-)\gcd(G,D_+)$ with coprime
factors; unnormalized, $\gcd(F(a,b),F(c,d))\mid\operatorname{lcm}(|D_-|,|D_+|)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
$p\nmid abcd$ since $F(a,b)$ is coprime to $ab$.  The bridge gives $p^e\mid D_-D_+$.  If
$p$ divided both channels then in $\mathbb F_p$ the ratios $r=a/b$, $s=c/d$ would satisfy
$r=s$ and $rs=1$, so $r^2=1$; $r=-1$ contradicts $r^2+3r+1=0$, and $r=1$ forces $p=5$.
Hence $p$ divides exactly one channel and, by coprimality, $p^e$ divides it.
\end{proof}

Both are \statuslean{} (\lean{bridge_identity}, \lean{fifth_trace_two_channel}).  For the
synchronized germ with $z_2=a/b$, $z_3=c/d$ reduced, the channels are the explicit
synchronized binomial gaps
\begin{equation}
 D_-\propto3^pM^q-2^pA^q=6^p(2^\delta-3^\delta),\qquad
 D_+\propto(MA)^q-6^p=6^p(6^\delta-1),
 \label{ct:eq-AE-channels}
\end{equation}
the first comparing the two branches in the same direction, the second a branch with the
reciprocal of the other.  Every shared prime power of the new normalized fifth-trace
factors is carried, with full valuation, by exactly one of them.  Exact examples:
$F(35,37)=11\cdot19\cdot31$, $F(64,65)=11\cdot31\cdot61$, with $31\mid D_-=-3\cdot31$ and
$11\mid D_+=-3\cdot5\cdot11$.

The theorem says where shared content must go, not that any is forced: real synchronization
does not transparently force modular synchronization.  The two channels are, however,
asymptotically disjoint, by an exact descent to the original gaps:

\begin{proposition}[Channel descent]\label{ct:prop-descent}
For all integers, $a(ad-bc)+b(ac-bd)=d(a^2-b^2)$ and $d(ac-bd)-c(ad-bc)=b(c^2-d^2)$.  Hence
any common divisor of the two channels divides $d(a^2-b^2)$ and $b(c^2-d^2)$, and a prime
$\ell\nmid6$ dividing both channels of \eqref{ct:eq-AE-channels} divides the doubled gaps
$M^{2q}-4^p=(M^q-2^p)(M^q+2^p)$ and $A^{2q}-9^p=(A^q-3^p)(A^q+3^p)$.
\end{proposition}

\statuslean{} (\lean{dvd_of_dvd_both_channels}, \lean{prime_dvd_doubled_gaps_of_dvd_both_channels}).
The pair $(M^{2q}/4^p,A^{2q}/9^p)$ lies in the fixed group $\langle(M,A),(2,3)\rangle$ with
multiplicatively independent coordinates, so the fixed-group Corvaja--Zannier bound of
Section~\ref{primetop:uniform-gcd} gives $\log\gcd(D_-,D_+)=o(q)$ for $\gcd$ taken prime to
$6$: shared channel support is, up to sign, shared support of the original synchronized
gaps, and it is asymptotically negligible.  Signed trace filters $\prod T_{d_i}^{c_i}$ can raise contact to
$2R$ exactly when $\sum_ic_i(d_i^{2r}-1)=0$ for $r<R$, which needs $m\ge R$ factors
(Vandermonde), and their cyclotomic degree budget $\sum_n|e_n|\varphi(n)$ grows much faster
than the contact (orders $4$ and $6$ already cost $10$ and $42$)---the trace-language form
of the finite-order height obstruction of Section~\ref{od:optimized}.

\begin{target}[Trace interfaces]\label{ct:target}
(i) Force shared normalized fifth-trace support along an infinite sequence of approximants
beyond what the two channels can carry; (ii) show that primes generated by the normalized
reciprocal quadratic have a local or Kummer signature incompatible with both
$3^pM^q-2^pA^q$ and $(MA)^q-6^p$ outside a negligible set; (iii) for $p\ge7$ compute the
bivariate common-root resultants of $P_p$ (the seventh-trace quartic factors over a
quadratic field) and classify the extension-field channels by Frobenius type.
\end{target}

\section{Exponent-lattice moment masks}
\label{sec:masks}

The last framework keeps the scalar viewpoint but changes variables: instead of the smooth
nodes it uses \emph{near-units attached to exponent-lattice relations}.  For
$\nu=(a,b)\in\Z^2$ put $\rho_\nu=2^a3^b=e^{\delta_\nu}$, $\delta_\nu=a\log2+b\log3$, and
