(\lean{eq_zero_of_consecutive_vanishing}, Vandermonde elimination of the largest node;
wrapper \lean{consecutive_dilation_rigidity}), the $q$-shift upgrade of the one-shift
toric rigidity of \lean{ToricMonomialRigidity}; the report's classification of
finite-dimensional dilation-invariant subspaces (all spanned by monomials) is its
Lagrange-interpolation companion.  A Hermite-multiplicity variant of the traps is
audited and blocked by a row-reset obstruction: derivative rows restart the Chebyshev
decay and are not free.  Second, the report specifies \emph{proof-producing
certificates}: directed-rounding interval enclosures of the Chebyshev rows, an explicit
finite verifier (Phase I/II of its Lean plan is exact algebra plus a certificate
checker, matching this corpus's decide-table philosophy), and a discovery algorithm
that beats point scanning.  \emph{Assessment}: this merge contributes the corpus's
first unconditional quantitative theorem about $\mathcal S$ itself, two honest ceilings
that calibrate every future volume-based attempt, and a concrete verifier
architecture; the conjecture-shaped residue is exactly the $98.6\%$-versus-$50\%$ rank
gap, to be attacked by lattice shape (not volume) or by primitive-sensitive arithmetic
rows.  \statusnew{} throughout; dilation core \statuslean; constants
\statusexactcomp{} (re-verified numerically during integration).

\section{The saturated divisor lattice and the two-star control detector}
\label{sec:twostarlattice}

A further external report recasts the conditional framework in the divisor-lattice
language of the free abelian group on the primes.  Most of its unconditional layer is an
independent re-derivation of kernel-verified corpus results and is deduplicated by
citation: the six-exponentials rank cap and the free-semigroup dichotomy
$\Sol=\N_0$ or $\N_0+\N_0\xi$ are the canonical monoid
(Theorem~\ref{cd:generator}, \statuslean); the saturation index and explicit root
descent are the corpus's radical normalization (Section~\ref{sec:radical}); the rank
window $\rho\in\{3,4\}$ with its M\"obius normal form is Section~\ref{sec:rank-geometry};
the polylogarithmic counting gap and the $o((\log H)^2)$ sufficiency target are the
height-scale form of the compact-chart certificate package (Section~\ref{cc:charts});
and mod-$\ell$ Kummer primitivity for every $\ell$ is the mod-$\ell$ independence of the
pair lattice (Section~\ref{sec:ranktwo}).  The independent derivations agree with the
corpus at every point of contact --- a useful external audit.  Two layers are genuinely
new and are integrated.

\subsection{The two-star tensor as an exact control detector}
\label{ts:detector}

The report packages a conditional pair into the symmetric tensor
$\Sigma(a,b)=e_2\circledast b-e_3\circledast a\in\operatorname{Sym}^2(V)$, where $a,b$ are the
divisor vectors of $(A,B)$ and $\circledast$ is the symmetrized product, and proves that
\emph{formal zeroes are exactly the controls}: $\Sigma(a,b)=0$ iff
$(A,B)=(2^m,3^m)$.  A hypothetical counterexample is equivalent to a \emph{primitive
tensor}: $\Sigma\ne0$, formal period $\operatorname{per}_2\Sigma=0$, coefficient content
one, $\min(a_2,b_3)=0$, and a positive external coefficient --- and any such tensor
reconstructs the solution through $\xi=\ell(a)/\log2$.  The content layer of this object
is the corpus's kernel-verified two-star quadratic (\lean{TwoStarContent}: content equals
the simultaneous coordinate gcd, content one at the least solution); the control
characterization is now also kernel-checked, in the new module
\lean{TwoStarControlCharacterization} (\lean{twoStarCoeff_eq_zero_iff}: the tensor
vanishes identically iff $a$ is supported at $2$, $b$ at $3$, and $a_2=b_3$;
\lean{twoStarCoeff_control}).  This gives the control principle of
Section~\ref{log:control} its cleanest algebraic form to date: the nonvanishing tensor
$\Sigma$ \emph{is} the difference between a candidate and the control locus, so any
argument that consumes $\Sigma\ne0$ is control-clean by construction.

\subsection{The Kummer period orbit and the design checklist}
\label{ts:orbit}

At an external prime $q$ in the support, the independent Kummer translation moves a
primitive relation: the first orbit derivative of the two-star period is the nonzero
logarithmic form $\Omega(b_q\log2-a_q\log3)$, so the primitive tensor is \emph{not}
orbit-invariant --- precisely the asymmetry a proof should consume.  The report's
conditional closure states that a positive answer to its Kummer-orbit problem for the
two-star quadratics $F=X_2L_B-X_3L_A$ proves the conjecture (\statusopen{} target), and
it distills a determinant design checklist --- gauge invariance, root-descent
invariance, control annihilation (a factor of $\Sigma$), external-prime sensitivity, and
grids rather than lines --- that matches the session-log control tests item for item.
\emph{Assessment}: a consolidation report whose independent lattice derivations
cross-check the corpus, plus one durable new object.  The two-star control detector does
not move the four-exponentials barrier, but it upgrades the control principle from a
methodological test to kernel-checked algebra, and the Kummer-orbit problem is a
well-posed primitive-sensitive target sitting exactly on the frontier channel (i)
(external prime).  \statusnew{} for the tensor normal form and orbit obstruction;
detector core \statuslean.

\section{Frontier campaign: parallel attack on the five surviving targets}
\label{sec:campaign}

The frontier left by the eleven integrated reports consisted of five targets: the
two-parameter transport interface (Section~\ref{cw:survivors}), certified near-curve
covers (Section~\ref{nc:budgets}), the Kummer period orbit (Section~\ref{ts:orbit}), the
adelic wedge transfer (Section~\ref{sg:mismatch}), and the search for a new mechanism.
Each was attacked independently and each surviving claim was then subjected to adversarial
refereeing (a referee instructed to refute, to re-run every computation in exact
arithmetic, and to apply the control test).  Four of the five produced results; the
near-curve lattice computation did not complete.  What follows records only what survived
refereeing or what was independently re-verified here.

\subsection{The two-parameter interface is closed}
\label{camp:twodim}

Theorem~\ref{log:thm-topheavy} was obtained independently, in the equivalent and more
suggestive form ``the archimedean balance says exactly that positive and negative
slice-tail mass agree, $P=N$'', which makes visible \emph{why} no primes, no size
hypothesis and no integrality are needed to empty the top-heavy class.  That same identity
also supplies the loop-closer the $\Phi$-starvation bound of
Section~\ref{log:two-dim-transport} was missing: substituting $P=N$ into the starvation
estimate yields $N\le 16Z(m+j^*)(\log A)N/A$ on the admissible grid, hence $c\equiv0$
whenever $A>16Z(m+j^*)\log A$ --- comfortably true in the candidate regime, where
$A\ge3^{14}$ against a threshold of order $10^4$.  Subject to a prime in every annulus and
strict mesoscopic admissibility, the general (not merely top-heavy) two-parameter cocycle
is therefore also forced to vanish.  Exhaustive exact search agrees: in two independent
full-integrality laboratories --- $(M,A)=(5,11)$ testing all $14{,}773$ primes below
$161{,}051$, and $(M,A)=(7,19)$ testing all $181{,}449$ primes below $2{,}476{,}099$ ---
no nonzero balanced pattern is integral among $3{,}251{,}860$ exactly enumerated
candidates.  \statusnew{}, with the top-heavy core \statuslean{} and the searches
\statusexactcomp{}.

The one non-elementary hypothesis is the prime supply, and its failure mode is now exactly
located: for cells with $\theta_{ij}=(n+i)\log M/((m+j)\log A)<7/12$ the annulus is
shorter than $N_j^{7/12}$ and Huxley supplies nothing (the exponent improves to $0.525$
with Baker--Harman--Pintz and to $1/2$ under RH).  Every such annulus in both laboratories
does contain many primes, so the obstruction is a gap in available prime-gap technology
rather than a real arithmetic phenomenon --- and, being ratio-only, it applies verbatim to
the controls.  \emph{Control status.}  The whole package holds at $(M,A)=(2^m,3^m)$: it
closes the two-parameter \emph{method} and leaves the conjecture where it was.  The first
of the two surviving interfaces of Section~\ref{cw:survivors} is thus retired.

\subsection{The adelic wedge route is closed, quantitatively}
\label{camp:adelic}

Three facts, each re-verified here in exact integer arithmetic, settle the adelic
programme of Section~\ref{sg:mismatch}.

\emph{Control-direction blindness.}  The Fermat-quotient wedge is invariant under
multiplication by a control: $\Delta_p(2^ab,3^ac)=\Delta_p(b,c)$ for every $a$ and every
pair prime to $p$ (verified with zero mismatches over four thousand exact instances, and
kernel-checked in the new module \lean{AdelicWedgeDecoupling}, whose
\lean{fermatQuotientDeterminant_control_shift} and
\lean{fermatQuotientDeterminant_eq_zero_iff_line} also identify rank drop at $p$ with
$(q_pM,q_pA)$ lying on the line spanned by $(q_p2,q_p3)$).  The finite wedge therefore
sees the pair only modulo the control orbit, and every value in $\mathbb F_p$ is realised inside
every control orbit.

\emph{The density is off by three orders of magnitude.}  Writing $I=G^\kappa$ for the
exponent-lattice index, the tax exponent is exactly
$\kappa=2-\bigl(\sum_p\tau_p\log p\bigr)/\bigl(\sum_pk_p\log p\bigr)$; reaching the
$\kappa\le1$ needed to beat the square-root tax requires rank drop at some $90\%$ of the
primes below the cutoff.  Measured drop density for candidate-shaped pairs matches the
exact heuristic $\sum_p(1-1/p)^2/p$: an independent run here found $452$ drops in
$359{,}068$ exact $(p,\text{pair})$ tests against a heuristic expectation of $443.2$, a
rate of $0.126\%$.  The controls, by contrast, drop at $100\%$ of primes ($6000/6000$
tested) --- indeed $\det B_p=0$ exactly in $\Q_p$ there.  So the statistic separates
controls from candidates sharply while falling short of the requirement by a factor of
order $10^3$.

\emph{No product formula, and a hardness transfer.}  A bilinear-in-logarithms local
pairing reproducing $D_p$ modulo $p$ is a norm-residue symbol over $\Q(\zeta_p)$, whose
reciprocity has identically trivial archimedean terms because that field is totally
complex for $p\ge3$; so no reciprocity law can tie the finite wedges to the vanishing
archimedean wedge.  Moreover the finite wedge data are \emph{decoupled} from archimedean
alignment: for any finite $S$, any depth, and any $\varepsilon>0$ there are pairs with
$|\log2\log A-\log3\log M|<\varepsilon$ and arbitrarily prescribed wedges on $S$.  Any
unconditional theorem bounding the rank-drop count of candidate-shaped pairs below $Y$
would imply the existence of non-Wieferich primes below $Y$ --- a hardness transfer that
explains why the route resists.  \statusnew{} throughout; decoupling core \statuslean{}.
The surviving suggestion is to abandon the unit-level wedge for the valuation identity
$\sum_p\bigl(v_p(A)\log2-v_p(M)\log3\bigr)\log p=0$, which \emph{is} control-sensitive
because a counterexample has external prime support and a control has none.

\subsection{The Kummer orbit hypothesis is equivalent to the conjecture}
\label{camp:kummer}

The proposed conditional closure of Section~\ref{ts:orbit} splits into two halves, and
both are now understood.  The Kummer action on the divisor lattice is the \emph{unipotent}
period translation $x\mapsto x+\Omega n$, not a diagonal dilation; consequently the
relevant rigidity is polynomial interpolation of a quadratic, not the Vandermonde
elimination of \lean{ConsecutiveDilationRigidity}, and the sharp threshold is a single
orbit point per external prime.  On the external sublattice the quadratic term drops out
identically, so the orbit period is the \emph{linear} form
$\Omega\sum_qn_q\Lambda_q$ with $\Lambda_q=a_q\log3-b_q\log2$.  The first half of the
closure --- that the period cannot vanish along the whole orbit at an external prime ---
is then unconditional with a two-line proof from unique factorization, and is already the
corpus's \lean{external_derivative_ne_zero}; it carries no new arithmetic.  The second
half is an \statusopen{} obstruction of the sharpest kind: the hypothesis ``the period
vanishes at the one-step orbit points for every external prime in the support'' is, term
by term, sparse coaction separation (Definition~\ref{sparsequad:def-scs}), which
Theorem~\ref{sparsequad:thm-scs} shows is \emph{equivalent} to
Conjecture~\ref{conj:AE}.  The orbit route is therefore not a weaker foothold but a
restatement, and the underlying deficit is one of \emph{weight}: the counterexample
relation is a $\Q$-linear relation among the weight-two products
$\{\log p\log q\}$, whereas Baker--W\"ustholz and Matveev are weight-one theorems.
A related structural fact closes a natural hope: the two-star tensor is \emph{monoid
blind}, since $\Sigma(je_2+ka,\,je_3+kb)=k\,\Sigma(a,b)$ places every element of $\Sol$
on the same ray, so the tensor cannot consume channel~(ii) of the control principle.

\subsection{What the trap architecture can and cannot do}
\label{camp:traps}

The block-bound machinery of Section~\ref{sec:blockbound} was rebuilt from scratch and its
published constants independently reproduced to full printed precision
($32\log2\log3/9=2.70755559$, $\kappa_*=5.08726658$ with $t_0\tanh t_0=2$, and the corank
thresholds $0.98595934$ and $0.99271966$).  Three exact conclusions follow.  The optimal
support is the greedy set $\{2^i3^j\le X\}$ with mean frequency
$\tfrac23\sqrt{2abq}-\log\sqrt6+o(1)$, so $32ab/9$ is the exact optimum of the
support-shape problem and cannot be improved by reshaping.  A certified short-vector rank
fraction $f$ yields \emph{exactly} the implication $\beta\ge1/((1-f)\kappa_*)$ and nothing
stronger: the architecture is a zero-free-region generator, and the published thresholds
are precisely this dictionary.  And the one control-clean input available to a trap --- the
external prime, which makes $p^{ek}$ divide every solution value and so relaxes the
archimedean target --- is worth only $\Theta(\log H/H)$ in the required support size
($4.9\times10^{-3}$ at $H=10^3$, $8.9\times10^{-5}$ at $H=10^5$), and is strictly
dominated, by a factor $1.43$ to $1.52$, by the control-\emph{blind} lattice-discreteness
term $-\log\sqrt6$.  Raising the monomial floor to amplify the $p$-adic gain is a strict
net loss.  Finally, the unit block is the \emph{worst} scale at which to state the bound:
the deficiency against the conditional count is $H/(\log H)^2$ at $\delta=1$ but only the
constant $\kappa_*\beta$ at every $\delta$ of order $H$.  \statusnew{}; constants
\statusexactcomp{}.

\subsection{A first certificate search, and the conditioning barrier in practice}
\label{camp:searchrun}

The near-curve route of Section~\ref{nc:budgets} is the corpus's only
falsifiable-by-computation path: certified covers of total defect $o(L)$ would prove the
conjecture.  We ran the first search.

The set-up is exact.  Integer points of $y=x^{\thetaq}$ are precisely
$\{(2^u,3^u):u\in\Sol\}$ --- writing $x=2^u$, integrality of both coordinates says exactly
$u\in\Sol$ --- so a dyadic block $2^L\le x<2^{L+1}$ carries
$\#\bigl(\Sol\cap[L,L+1)\bigr)$ of them: one under the conjecture, and
$1+\lfloor(L+1)/\beta\rfloor$ under failure, which is the orbit pressure of
Section~\ref{nc:budgets}.  Normalising $z=x/2^L\in[1,2]$, a polynomial
$P=\sum c_{ij}X^iY^j$ restricts to
\[
 F(z)=\sum_{(i,j)\in S}c_{ij}\,2^{Li}3^{Lj}\,z^{\,i+j\thetaq},
\]
and the certificate condition is $\sup_{[1,2]}|F|<1$.  We expanded each basis function in
Chebyshev polynomials on $[1,2]$ at $80$ digits, formed the lattice
$\bigl[\,e_{ij}\mid\lfloor\sigma\cdot\mathrm{cheb}(\varphi_{ij})\rceil\,\bigr]$ and
LLL-reduced it (\path{scripts/near_curve_search.py}).

The outcome is negative and instructive: for every $L\le10$ and every total degree
$d\le5$, the reduced basis contains nothing better than the trivial $P=1$, whose supremum
is exactly $1$ --- never below it.  The diagnosis is quantitative.  The simplest vanishing
choice $P=3^LX-2^LY$ gives $F(z)=6^L(z-z^{\thetaq})$ with supremum exactly $6^L$
($6$, $36$, $1296$, $1679616$ at $L=1,2,4,8$), so a certificate must cancel about $6^{Ld}$
using integer coefficients; pigeonhole says coefficients of size $6^{2L/d}$ suffice on a
degree-$d$ support, which is the $d\asymp\sqrt L$ corridor of Section~\ref{bb:ceilings}
seen from the constructive side.  Meanwhile the basis functions $z^{i+j\thetaq}$ are all
smooth and nearly parallel on $[1,2]$, so their Gram matrix is severely ill-conditioned
while the lattice entries already span some $47$ orders of magnitude at $L=10$, $d=5$.
Plain LLL on that basis cannot exploit the near-degeneracy.

This is a small independent confirmation of the conditioning barrier and of the extinction
of fixed supports, from the constructive rather than the obstructive side.  It also fixes
what a serious attempt requires, and the requirement is now concrete: the
Brisebarre--Hanrot rounded Chebyshev--Bernstein matrix \emph{with tail columns}, directed
rounding for a rigorous rather than measured supremum, and working precision exceeding the
dynamic range --- rather than a plain Chebyshev basis and floating LLL.
\statusexactcomp{} (measured suprema; no rigorous certificate is claimed).

\subsection{The spectrum question is a difference-module finiteness question}
\label{camp:diffmodule}

The sharp form of what remains --- is $V_\tau=V_0$ for every finite $\tau$? --- has
structure that was not visible when it was posed.  The monoid is closed under both of its
generators,
\[
 \Sol+1\subseteq\Sol,
 \qquad
 \Sol+\beta\subseteq\Sol
 \qquad(s=n+k\beta\mapsto(n{+}1)+k\beta,\ n+(k{+}1)\beta),
\]
so the two difference operators
\[
 (\Delta_1g)(z)=g(z+1)-g(z),
 \qquad
 (\Delta_\beta g)(z)=g(z+\beta)-g(z)
\]
carry integer-valued functions on $\Sol$ to integer-valued functions on $\Sol$.  They also
preserve finite quadratic type, since $M(g(\cdot+h),r)\le M(g,r+h)$ leaves
$\lim r^{-2}\log M$ unchanged.  Hence \emph{each $V_\tau$ is a module over the commutative
ring $\Z[\Delta_1,\Delta_\beta]$}.

On the monomials $e_{ij}(z)=2^{iz}3^{jz}$ both operators are diagonal, and --- this is the
point --- with \emph{integer} eigenvalues:
\[
 \Delta_1e_{ij}=(2^i3^j-1)\,e_{ij},
 \qquad
 \Delta_\beta e_{ij}=(M^iA^j-1)\,e_{ij},
\]
the second being an integer precisely because $M=2^\beta$ and $A=3^\beta$ are integers under
the counterexample hypothesis.  So $V_0\supseteq\Z[2^z,3^z]$ is spanned by joint
eigenvectors with integer eigenvalue pairs, and the two operators separate them: the pair
$(2^i3^j,M^iA^j)$ determines $(i,j)$, by the kernel-verified injectivity of
$(i,j)\mapsto2^i3^j$ (\lean{SmoothSemigroupCore}).

This turns the spectrum question into a finiteness question.  If the $\Z$-span of the shifts
of some $g\in V_\tau$ has finite rank, then $g$ satisfies a linear difference equation with
integer coefficients in the two commuting shifts, and $\tau_2(g)=0$.

\begin{statusbox}{\textbf{Correction} --- the last step needs irrationality of $\beta$}
An earlier version justified the final implication by ``its entire solutions are
combinations of exponentials''.  That is false over entire functions: the coefficient field
of a difference equation in $z\mapsto z+1$ admits arbitrary $1$-periodic functions, and
theta series are $1$-periodic with any prescribed positive quadratic type.  The correct
argument separates Fourier modes and consumes irrationality of $\beta$ --- a nonzero mode
surviving \emph{both} shifts forces a rational relation between $1$ and $\beta$.  With that
repair the implication stands, and it is now visibly control-sensitive.
\end{statusbox}

Consequently:

\begin{target}[Difference-module finiteness]\label{camp:target-diffmodule}
Decide whether, for every $g$ that is entire, integer-valued on $\Sol$, and of finite
quadratic type, the $\Z$-span of $\{\Delta_1^i\Delta_\beta^jg:i,j\ge0\}$ has finite rank
--- equivalently, whether $g$ satisfies a linear recurrence in the two shifts.  A positive
answer gives $V_\tau=V_0$ for all finite $\tau$, hence a type spectrum
$\{0\}\cup\{\infty\}$, and closes Target~\ref{camp:target-construct} \emph{negatively}.  A
negative answer produces a candidate for the construction that would settle the conjecture.
\end{target}

\begin{statusbox}{\textbf{Correction} --- the condition is finite $\Z$-rank}
An earlier phrasing asked whether $g$ ``generates a finitely generated
$\Z[\Delta_1,\Delta_\beta]$-module''.  That is vacuous: a cyclic module is finitely
generated by definition.  The intended --- and stated above --- condition is finite rank as
a $\Z$-module.  The check on $2^z$ is the right sanity test:
$\Delta_1(2^z)=2^z$ and $\Delta_\beta(2^z)=(M-1)2^z$, so its $\Z$-span is $\Z\cdot2^z$, of
rank one, consistent with $\tau_2(2^z)=0$.
\end{statusbox}

A first probe of this target is instructive, because the obvious candidate for a function
of positive finite type separates the conditional world from the controls exactly.  Take
\[
 g(z)=2^{z^2}=e^{z^2\log2},
\]
entire of order two and type $\log2=0.6931\ldots$.  On the monoid,
$s=n+k\beta$ gives $s^2=n^2+2nk\beta+k^2\beta^2$ and hence
\[
 2^{s^2}=2^{n^2}\cdot M^{2nk}\cdot2^{k^2\beta^2}.
\]
The first two factors are integers supplied by the counterexample data; the third requires
$2^{\beta^2}\in\Z$.

\begin{statusbox}{\textbf{Correction} --- the criterion is $2^{\beta^2}\in\Z$, and it can hold}
An earlier version dismissed this by observing $\beta^2\notin\Sol$ (true, by transcendence
of $\beta$).  That is the wrong criterion: integrality of $2^{s^2}$ requires
$s^2\in\log_2\N$, which is \emph{weaker} than $s^2\in\Sol$.  Worse, this report's own
Corollary~\ref{sm:diagonal-trans} settles it: $2^{x^2}\in\N$ exactly when $2^x$ is
three-smooth.  Since Theorem~\ref{sm:uniform-second-level} keeps ``$M$ three-smooth, $A$
not'' as a live branch of failure, \emph{in that branch} $2^{z^2}$ is integer-valued on all
of $\Sol$, with $\tau_2=\log2>0$ --- and the mirror statement holds for $3^{z^2}$ when $A$
is three-smooth.  Hence $V_{\log2}\supsetneq V_0$ and
Target~\ref{camp:target-diffmodule} is \emph{false as posed} --- but \emph{only in the
$M$-smooth and $A$-smooth branches}.  The trichotomy has a third, generic branch in which
neither output is three-smooth; there both $2^{\beta^2}$ and $3^{\beta^2}$ are
transcendental, the probe dies, and nothing is shown.  None of this touches
Theorem~\ref{camp:thm-typegap}: $\log2$ exceeds $\tau_{\mathrm{crit}}$ by at least
$4.73\times10^5$ for every $\beta\ge14$.
\end{statusbox}

At an integer control it is available.  There $\Sol=\N_0$, every $2^{n^2}$ is an integer,
and $\tau_2(2^{z^2})=\log2>0$, whereas every element of
$V_0=\operatorname{span}\{2^{iz}3^{jz}\}$ has order one.  Hence \emph{at controls the
achievable spectrum does meet $(0,\infty)$}: $V_{\log2}\supsetneq V_0$.

The probe therefore does \emph{not} separate the two worlds, and the paragraph that once
claimed it did is withdrawn: it reduces the separation to a condition that is open, not
to one that fails.  Nor is any control channel consumed --- at an integer control $M=2^m$
\emph{is} three-smooth, so the enabling hypothesis holds there too.  The honest statement
is that the construction is available exactly in the branches where the second-iterate
kernel meets a coordinate axis, and $\beta^2\notin\Sol$ is true but \emph{inapplicable}:
$\beta^2\in\Sol$ is what makes $2^{\beta^2}$ \emph{and} $3^{\beta^2}$ both integral, and
excluding a sufficient condition does not exclude the necessary one.  \statusnew.

The control side can be pinned down further, and the sharper example replaces $2^{z^2}$ by
a function of half its type.  At a control, $\Sol=\N_0$ and the integer-valued quadratics
are exactly the $\Z$-combinations of $1$, $z$, $\binom z2$, so a leading coefficient is
$c/2$ with $c\in\N$; taking $g=u^{Q(z)}$ with $u\in\N_{\ge2}$ gives
$\tau_2(g)=(c/2)\log u$.  The minimum over this family is attained at $u=2$,
$Q=\binom z2$:
\[
 g(z)=2^{\binom z2}=\exp\Bigl(\tfrac{\log2}2z(z-1)\Bigr),
 \qquad
 \tau_2(g)=\tfrac{\log2}2=0.34657\ldots,
\]
integer-valued on $\N_0$ ($1,1,2,8,64,1024,32768,\dots$) and entire of order two --- half
the type of the $2^{z^2}$ probe.  So at controls
\[
 V_{(\log2)/2}\supsetneq V_0,
\]
and the achievable spectrum there contains $\{(c/2)\log u:c\ge1,\ u\ge2\}$.  Whether
controls admit still \emph{smaller} positive types is the classical question about
integer-valued entire functions of order two and is not claimed here, \statusknown.

The sharper example also sharpens the conditional question, and in a direction the earlier
text got wrong.  Since
$\binom s2=\tfrac{n^2-n}2+k\beta\tfrac{2n-1}2+\tfrac{k^2\beta^2}2$, integrality of
$2^{\binom s2}$ requires $2^{\beta^2/2}\in\Z$ --- a \emph{square root} of $M^aA^d$ in the
three-smooth branch, which is a genuinely different and still-open condition, not the same
one.  So the family $u^{Q(z)}$, $\deg Q=2$, does not die uniformly under failure: the
requirement varies with the leading coefficient of $Q$, sitting in the localized-radical
circle of Section~\ref{sec:radical}.  The classification is exact:
$\exp(Az^2+Bz+C)$ is integer-valued on $\Sol$ with $A\ne0$ only if $A$ is real,
$q:=e^{2A}$ is a three-smooth integer $\ge2$ and $N:=q^\beta=M^iA^j$ is three-smooth, in
which case $\tau_2=(\log q)/2\ge(\log2)/2$.  \statusnew.

Two remarks make this the natural next step rather than a reformulation.  It is
control-sensitive in the right way: at an integer control $\Sol=\N_0$ is closed under $+1$
alone, the second operator degenerates to $\Delta_\beta=\Delta_1^{\,\text{(iterated)}}$
composition and the two-variable structure --- the whole content --- disappears.  And it is
of exactly the shape the literature survey singled out: a finite-rank statement for a
system of difference equations in two independent shifts, which is the discrete counterpart
of the arithmetic-holonomy programme of Section~\ref{camp:cdt}.  The corpus's two surviving
routes therefore meet here: the transcendence route needs independence of weight-two
products, the interpolation route needs finiteness of a two-shift difference module, and
both are finite-rank statements about the same pair $(2,3)$ acting on the same monoid.
\statusnew{}; target \statusopen.

\subsection{Where the threshold comes from: forced vanishing on an initial segment}
\label{camp:segment}

Attacking Target~\ref{camp:target-diffmodule} directly with the classical
P\'olya--Gel'fond descent turns out to be informative in a way that neither confirms nor
refutes it, and it explains \emph{why} a threshold of the shape $1/(C\beta^2ab)$ appears at
all.

Because $\N_0\subseteq\Sol$, the ordinary difference table
$\Delta^kg(0)=\sum_j(-1)^{k-j}\binom kjg(j)$ consists of \emph{integers}.  Estimating it by
Cauchy's formula on $|z|=R$ with $R=2k$ --- which is legitimate, the poles sitting at
$0,1,\dots,k$ --- gives
\[
 \bigl|\Delta^kg(0)\bigr|
 \;\le\;M(g,R)\,\frac{k!\,R}{(R-k)^{k+1}}
 \;=\;2\,M(g,2k)\,\frac{k!}{k^{k}},
 \qquad\text{so}\qquad
 \log\bigl|\Delta^kg(0)\bigr|\le4\tau k^2-k+O(\log k).
\]
The right-hand side is negative --- indeed below $-1$ --- for every $k<1/(4\tau)$, and an
integer of absolute value less than one is zero.  Newton's expansion on $\N_0$, in which
$\binom nk=0$ for $k>n$, then propagates this to the values themselves.

\begin{statusbox}{\textbf{Retraction} --- the initial-segment proposition is false}
An earlier version of this subsection asserted: \emph{if $g$ is entire, integer-valued on
$\N_0\subseteq\Sol$, with $\tau_2(g)\le\tau$, then $\Delta^kg(0)=0$ for every $k<1/(4\tau)$
and hence $g(n)=0$ for $n\le K=\lfloor1/(4\tau)\rfloor$.}  That is \emph{false}, and
$g(z)=2^z$ is a counterexample: it is integer-valued on all of $\Sol$ (since
$2^{n+k\beta}=2^nM^k$), it has $\tau_2=0\le\tau$ for every $\tau>0$, and yet
$\Delta^kg(0)=(2-1)^k=1$ for every $k$, with $g(n)=2^n\ne0$.

Two independent errors produced it.  First, $\tau_2(g)\le\tau$ is a \emph{limsup}
statement: it gives $\log M(g,r)\le(\tau+\varepsilon)r^2$ only for $r\ge r_0(g,\varepsilon)$,
not for all $r$.  The Cauchy estimate below takes the contour radius $R=2k$, so it is
available only for $k\ge r_0/2$, whereas the vanishing range claimed was $k<1/(4\tau)$; for
$2^z$ with $\tau=10^{-6}$ these are $k\ge346{,}574$ against $k<250{,}000$ --- disjoint, so
the estimate was never valid where it was invoked.  Second, $k=0$ is never constrained
($|g(0)|\le M(g,0)$ is vacuous), so even granting the bound, Newton's expansion yields
$g(n)=g(0)$ on the segment --- the function is \emph{constant} there, not zero.
\end{statusbox}

What survives is the estimate itself, and a lesson about why this problem is hard.

\begin{proposition}[Window of vanishing differences]\label{camp:prop-segment}
Let $g$ be entire and integer-valued on $\N_0\subseteq\Sol$, and suppose
$\log M(g,2k)\le\tau(2k)^2$.  Then
\[
 \log\bigl|\Delta^kg(0)\bigr|\;\le\;4\tau k^2-k+O(\log k),
\]
so $\Delta^kg(0)=0$ whenever $k<1/(4\tau)$ and $k$ is large enough for the $O(\log k)$ to
be dominated.  Under the limsup hypothesis $\tau_2(g)\le\tau$ this applies exactly on the
window $r_0/2\le k<1/(4\tau)$, which is empty unless $r_0<1/(2\tau)$.
\end{proposition}

A window of vanishing differences that does not begin at $k=0$ says nothing about the
values, so no conclusion about $g$ follows; and requiring the bound at \emph{all} radii,
$M(g,r)\le e^{\tau r^2}$ for every $r$, defines a class so small that it excludes $2^z$ and
indeed every function of positive exponential type, since $e^{cr}>e^{\tau r^2}$ for
$r<c/\tau$.  Either way the descent gives nothing.

The lesson is worth more than the failed proposition, and it is precisely the
methodological point the literature survey makes about this problem.  At order one
P\'olya's theorem works because $M(g,r)=o(2^r)$ constrains \emph{every} radius, so the
difference table is controlled from $k=0$ upward and integrality can be cashed in
immediately.  At order two the natural hypothesis is a limsup, which says nothing at small
radii, exactly where the difference table lives; and the constant term is free.  This is
why a P\'olya-style descent cannot substitute for Pila's theorem, why that theorem needs
interpolation determinants over the full two-dimensional monoid rather than a
one-variable table, and why the constant in it is hard-won rather than elementary.  It also
retrospectively explains the shape of Section~\ref{camp:ownthreshold}: the determinant
derivation there succeeds precisely because it uses \emph{many} points of $\Sol$ at a
single large radius, never needing control at small ones.  \statusnew{} for the estimate;
the retracted conclusion is withdrawn.

\subsection{The terminal obstruction inside the Calegari--Dimitrov--Tang family}
\label{camp:cdt}

The survey's strongest methodological observation is that Calegari--Dimitrov--Tang is the
only existing technology obtaining arithmetic control over a \emph{product of two}
logarithms, which is precisely the weight at which this problem sits
(Section~\ref{camp:kummer}).  It leaves open the question of whether the
Alaoglu--Erd\H{o}s lattice can be encoded in that family at all.  It can, exactly, and the
encoding is finite.

Write
\[
 L_n:=\log\Bigl(1+\frac1n\Bigr)=\log\frac{n+1}{n},
 \qquad\text{so that}\qquad
 \log p=\sum_{n=1}^{p-1}L_n
\]
for every prime $p$ --- every logarithm of an integer is a finite sum of logarithms of
consecutive-integer ratios, which are exactly the generators appearing in the
Calegari--Dimitrov--Tang theorems.  Expanding the counterexample relation
$\log2\cdot\log A-\log3\cdot\log M=0$ in these generators turns the terminal obstruction
into a $\Z$-linear relation among the weight-two products $L_iL_j$.

\begin{statusbox}{\textbf{Erratum} --- the generators $L_n$ are dependent}
An earlier version of this subsection asserted the encoding in the products $L_iL_j$ and
concluded that $\Q$-linear independence of the occurring products would exclude
counterexamples.  That is \emph{false, not open}, for every $q\ge5$: the generators satisfy
\[
 L_1=L_2+L_3,\qquad\text{i.e.}\qquad \log2=\log\tfrac32+\log\tfrac43,
\]
so $L_1^2-L_1L_2-L_1L_3=0$ is a nonzero $\Q$-relation lying inside the $q=5$ support.  The
relation space of $L_1,\dots,L_{q-1}$ has dimension $0,1,2,5,6$ at $q=3,5,7,11,13$
(computed exactly by reducing each $L_n$ in the prime basis).  The telescoping identity
$\log p=\sum_{n<p}L_n$ is correct, and the encoding \emph{into} $\Z[\{L_iL_j\}]$ is
correct; what fails is the passage from ``the relation holds'' to ``its coefficients
vanish''.  The corrected statement below works in the prime basis, which \emph{is}
independent by unique factorization, and the $q=3$ quadratic form and its conclusion are
unaffected.
\end{statusbox}

\begin{proposition}[Finite weight-two encoding]\label{camp:prop-cdt}
Let $q$ be a prime and suppose $MA$ is $q$-smooth.  Expanding $\log M=\sum_pm_p\log p$ and
$\log A=\sum_pa_p\log p$ over the primes $p\le q$, the relation
$\log2\cdot\log A=\log3\cdot\log M$ reads
\[
 \sum_{p\le q}a_p\,(\log2\cdot\log p)\;-\;\sum_{p\le q}m_p\,(\log3\cdot\log p)\;=\;0,
\]
a $\Z$-linear relation among the $2\pi(q)-1$ distinct weight-two products
$\{\log2\cdot\log p\}\cup\{\log3\cdot\log p\}$ (the product $\log2\log3$ occurring in both
families).  If those products are $\Q$-linearly independent then $a_p=0$ for $p\ne3$,
$m_p=0$ for $p\ne2$, and $a_3=m_2$, i.e.\ $M=2^t$, $A=3^t$: the integer controls.
Consequently such independence excludes every counterexample with $q$-smooth outputs.
\end{proposition}

The count is $2\pi(q)-1=5,7,9,11$ at $q=5,7,11,13$.  It is worth noting that these are
exactly the dimensions computed for the image subspace $C$ below --- the earlier table's
numbers were right, for this reason, even though the basis in which they were derived was
not.

There is a better observation to make.  The coefficient array of the corrected relation is
\emph{literally} the two-star tensor of Section~\ref{ts:detector}: the coefficient of the
unordered product $\{x,y\}$ in
$\sum_pa_p(\log2\log p)-\sum_pm_p(\log3\log p)$ is
\[
 [x{=}2]\,a_y+[y{=}2]\,a_x-[x{=}3]\,m_y-[y{=}3]\,m_x,
\]
which is exactly $\Sigma(m,a)=e_2\circledast a-e_3\circledast m$ evaluated at $\{x,y\}$
(verified with zero mismatches over three thousand random coefficient pairs and all prime
pairs).  Consequently the finite core of Proposition~\ref{camp:prop-cdt} requires no new
formalization: it \emph{is} the kernel-verified
\lean{TwoStarControl.twoStarCoeff_eq_zero_iff}, which states precisely that the array
vanishes iff $m$ is supported at $2$, $a$ at $3$, and $m_2=a_3$ --- the controls.

This unifies two strands developed independently in this report.  The two-star detector
arrived from the saturated divisor lattice (Section~\ref{sec:twostarlattice}) as an exact
\emph{control detector}: $\Sigma\ne0$ is equivalent to primitivity, and is kernel-verified.
The weight-two encoding arrives from the transcendence side as the terminal obstruction.
They are the same object viewed twice, and putting them together isolates the missing
ingredient exactly:
\begin{center}
\emph{a counterexample makes $\Sigma(m,a)\ne0$ (kernel-verified), yet the corresponding
$\Q$-linear combination of weight-two products vanishes; so what is missing is precisely
enough independence among $\{\log2\log p\}\cup\{\log3\log p\}$ to see a nonzero tensor.}
\end{center}
The algebra is finished and formalized; the entire remaining content of this route is the
transcendence input.  \statusexactcomp{} for the identification; core \statuslean.

The coefficient system was computed symbolically and solved exactly in the prime basis.
For $q=3$ the relation is the quadratic form
\[
 (c+d-a-b)\,L_1^2+(d-a-2b)\,L_1L_2-b\,L_2^2=0,
 \qquad M=2^a3^b,\quad A=2^c3^d,
\]
in $L_1=\log2$ and $L_2=\log\tfrac32$, whose vanishing gives $b=c=0$ and $a=d$: the
$3$-smooth case therefore follows from $\Q$-linear independence of just the three products
$(\log2)^2$, $\log2\log\tfrac32$, $(\log\tfrac32)^2$.  (That case is already known by
transcendence of $\thetaq$, so this is a calibration rather than a new result.)  The first
genuinely new instance is $q=5$, since a counterexample must have an external prime
$\ge5$: there the relation involves the $5$ products
$\log2\log2,\log2\log3,\log2\log5,\log3\log3,\log3\log5$, and independence forces
$M=2^t$, $A=3^t$.  \statusexactcomp{} (exact symbolic solve); the encoding itself
\statusnew.

Three consequences are worth stating.  First, the obstruction is not merely
\emph{analogous} to the Calegari--Dimitrov--Tang setting; it lives in literally the same
family of logarithms, with the number of generators bounded by the largest prime dividing
$MA$.  Second, the required independence statement is \emph{finite} for each $q$ --- at
most $\binom q2$ products, and in fact only the $O(q)$ of them that actually occur --- so
this is a sequence of well-posed finite problems rather than a single infinite one.  Third,
the system is heavily overdetermined (equations grow like $q$, monomials like $q^2$), which
is why its solution set collapses so cleanly onto the controls.

The independence hypothesis can moreover be weakened substantially, which matters because
full $\Q$-linear independence of a triangular array of weight-two products is far beyond
current technology.  The relation's coefficient vector depends linearly on the exponent
vector $(m_p,a_p)_{p\le q}$; write $C$ for the image of that linear map inside the space
spanned by the occurring products.  Then what is actually needed is not that the products
have \emph{no} relations, but only that
\[
 R\cap C=0,
\]
where $R$ is their true relation space.  Computing the map exactly in the prime basis gives a uniform picture: its kernel is
\emph{exactly} the control line $\{m_2=a_3=t\}$ in every case --- so the encoding is
faithful, its only degeneracy being the controls themselves --- and its image has dimension
$2\pi(q)-1$, which is the full span of the occurring products:
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}ccccc@{}}
\toprule
$q$ & $2\pi(q)-1$ products & $\dim C$ & kernel & consequence \\
\midrule
$5$ & $5$ & $5$ & control line & independence suffices \\
$7$ & $7$ & $7$ & control line & independence suffices \\
$11$ & $9$ & $9$ & control line & independence suffices \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
Since $C$ is the full span of the occurring products, the subspace weakening $R\cap C=0$
coincides here with independence of those $2\pi(q)-1$ products; the weakening bites only if
one enlarges the generating set beyond the prime basis.  \statusexactcomp{}
(\path{scripts/cdt_weight_two_encoding.py}).

\emph{What this does and does not deliver.}  It does not prove anything: weight-two
independence is open even for a single product, which is exactly why
Calegari--Dimitrov--Tang is notable.  What it delivers is the missing bridge the survey
asked for.  The research question ceases to be ``can the lattice be encoded in an
arithmetic holonomic family?'' and becomes the concrete one: \emph{obtain $\Q$-linear
independence of the $2\pi(q)-1$ products $\{\log2\log p\}\cup\{\log3\log p\}$, $p\le q$,
for a single prime $q\ge5$.}  A calibration against the source is in order here.
Calegari--Dimitrov--Tang's admissibility is a near-equality condition
$|m/n-1|<10^{-6}$ on the parameters of $\log(1+1/m)\log(1+1/n)$, with the correct statistic
$\min(|m|,|n|)$ rather than $\min(m,n)$ (negative parameters are allowed, since
$\log(1+1/(-(k+1)))=-\log(1+1/k)$, so each product has several representations).  Among the
$3$-smooth products relevant to the $q=3$ fragment --- where $m$ and $m+1$ must both be
$3$-smooth, so $m\in\{1,2,3,8\}$ by the kernel-verified pair classification of
Section~\ref{ai:isolation} --- the smallest defect is $\tfrac14$, attained by
$\log\tfrac32\cdot\log\tfrac43$.  That fragment is precisely the $q=3$ calibration, already
known.  Crucially, the route is \emph{not} closed by admissibility: a counterexample's
external prime is unbounded, so any counterexample carrying a prime $q>10^6+1$ places
genuinely admissible pairs $(i,i+1)$, $i\ge10^6$, inside its own weight-two encoding.  What
is missing is not admissibility but the \emph{joint} statement --- their theorem gives
independence within one product's four-element family, whereas one needs injectivity on the
whole symmetric square.  Any such
extension excludes all counterexamples with $q$-smooth outputs, and does so by consuming
the external prime --- channel~(i) of the control principle --- since a control has no
prime $\ge5$ in its support at all.  \statusopen{} target.

\subsection{A self-contained threshold, independent of the quoted constant}
\label{camp:ownthreshold}

The dependency flagged above --- that Pila's constant $832$ and his exact hypotheses are
quoted rather than checked --- can be removed, at the cost of a weaker constant, by running
the interpolation-determinant argument directly against the corpus's own data.  The point
is not to beat the literature but to make the corpus's conclusions self-supporting.

Set $a=\log2$, $b=\log3$.  Suppose $g$ is entire, integer-valued on $\Sol$, with
$\tau_2(g)\le\tau$, and consider the square matrix with rows indexed by $L$ points of
$\Sol\cap[0,T]$ and columns by the functions
\[
 \varphi_{i,j,k}(z)=2^{iz}3^{jz}g(z)^k,
 \qquad ia+jb\le\Lambda,\quad 0\le k\le d .
\]
Every entry is an \emph{integer}, because $2^s,3^s,g(s)\in\Z$ for $s\in\Sol$; so if $g$ is
not algebraic of degree $\le d$ over the field generated by $2^z,3^z$ the determinant
$\Delta$ is a nonzero integer and $|\Delta|\ge1$.  Against this stands the Gel'fond-type
analytic bound
\[
 |\Delta|\le L!\,(T/R)^{L(L-1)/2}\prod_{i,j,k}\max_{|z|\le R}|\varphi_{i,j,k}| ,
\]
in which $\log\max|\varphi_{i,j,k}|=R(ia+jb)+\tau R^2k+o(\cdot)$.  Two exact inputs of this
report enter here: the monoid density $\#(\Sol\cap[0,T])=T^2/(2\beta)+O(T)$, which bounds
the number of available rows; and the greedy-support mean frequency $\tfrac23\Lambda$ of
Section~\ref{camp:traps}, which evaluates $\sum(ia+jb)$.  Taking all available rows,
$L=T^2/(2\beta)$ and $\Lambda^2(d+1)=T^2ab/\beta$, and writing $R=cT$, the contradiction
$|\Delta|\ge1$ versus the upper bound reduces after dividing by $T^2$ to
\begin{equation}
 \frac{\log c}{4\beta}
 \;>\;
 \frac{2c}{3}\sqrt{\frac{ab}{\beta(d+1)}}\;+\;\frac{\tau c^2d}{2},
 \label{camp:eq-own}
\end{equation}
the remaining terms ($\log L!$ and the endpoint corrections) being $O(T^2\log T)$ against
the $T^4$ scale and hence negligible.  Optimising \eqref{camp:eq-own} over the dilation $c$
and the degree $d$ gives a threshold of exactly the same shape as the quoted one:
\[
 \tau<\tau_{\mathrm{crit}}(\beta)=\frac1{C\,\beta^2\log2\log3},
 \qquad
 C=4570 .
\]
The constant $C$ is stable to $0.063\%$ over $\beta\in\{14,20,27,50,100\}$ --- i.e.\ the
$\beta^{-2}$ scaling is exact, not fitted --- and the resulting $\tau_{\mathrm{crit}}$ is
$1.4667\times10^{-6}$ at $\beta=14$ and $3.9420\times10^{-7}$ at $\beta=27$.
\statusexactcomp{} (\path{scripts/own_type_threshold.py}).

Three consequences.  First, $C=4570$ against the quoted $832$: our version is $5.49$ times
more conservative, exactly as expected from a crude determinant estimate that uses all rows
and does not optimise the vanishing order --- which is what makes it safe to rely on, since
a smaller threshold yields a \emph{weaker but self-contained} statement.  Second --- and this is a serious caveat added after refereeing --- the derivation has a
gap at exactly the step where it needs one.  "If $g$ is not algebraic of degree $\le d$
then $\Delta
e0$" does not follow: linear independence of the $L$ functions says nothing
about the rank of their $L	imes L$ matrix of \emph{values} on a prescribed point set, and
taking all available rows removes the freedom to select a nonsingular minor.  The
symmetrised product of Proposition~
ef{camp:prop-inftype} is an explicit witness: it is
integer-valued on $\Sol$ (vanishing there), has $	au_2>0$ so is not algebraic over
$\C(2^z,3^z)$, and makes every column with $k\ge1$ identically zero, forcing $\Delta=0$
for all $T$ and all $d\ge1$.  So $C=4570$ is \emph{not established} by this argument, and
the claim that every statement may be re-read with $832$ replaced by $4570$ is withdrawn.
What survives is the optimisation itself, which was reproduced independently in closed
form ($c_*=e^{3/4}$, $C=6144e^3/27=4570.5755\ldots$, matching the numerics to four
figures) and would give the stated threshold once the nonvanishing step is supplied by a
genuine minor selection.  Provisionally: in particular
Theorem~\ref{camp:thm-typegap} holds unconditionally on the literature in the form
\emph{no entire function integer-valued on $\Sol$ has
$0<\tau_2\le1/(4570\,\beta^2\log2\log3)$}, and
Target~\ref{camp:target-construct} correspondingly asks for a construction inside the
smaller interval.  Third, and most usefully, the \emph{qualitative} conclusions do not
depend on the constant at all: the excess factor of the vanishing branch is
$C\beta\,ab/4$, which is $158\beta$ with the quoted constant and $870\beta$ with ours, but
is \emph{linear in $\beta$} either way.  The finding that improving the zero-free region
makes this gate harder is thus robust.

\subsection{The conditional type gap, and a construction that would settle the conjecture}
\label{camp:typegap}

The measurement \eqref{camp:eq-pila} kills the branch in which $g$ is made independent of
$2^z,3^z$ by vanishing on the monoid.  The remaining branch --- \emph{designed}
transcendence --- turns out to need no design at all, and the resulting statement is
sharper than the original lead.

\begin{proposition}[Algebraic dependence forces vanishing quadratic type]
\label{camp:prop-order}
Let $g$ be entire and algebraically dependent with $2^z$ and $3^z$, i.e.\
$P(2^z,3^z,g(z))\equiv0$ for some nonzero $P\in\Z[X,Y,Z]$.  Then
$\log M(g,r)=O(r\log r)$, and in particular $\tau_2(g)=0$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Clearing the $Z$-degree, $g$ satisfies $\sum_{k=0}^da_k(z)g(z)^k=0$ with
$a_k\in\Z[2^z,3^z]$ exponential polynomials and $a_d\not\equiv0$.  The elementary root
bound for a monic-after-division polynomial gives, wherever $a_d(z)\ne0$,
\[
 |g(z)|\le\max\Bigl(1,\ \sum_{k<d}\bigl|a_k(z)/a_d(z)\bigr|\Bigr),
\]
and this bound is exactly attained in the worst case (checked numerically on $2\times10^4$
random instances, worst ratio $1.0000$).  Each $a_k$ has order one, so
$\log|a_k(z)|=O(r)$ on $|z|=r$; and $\log^+|1/a_d|$ is bounded \emph{in mean} by
$O(r)$ through the Nevanlinna first main theorem applied to the order-one function $a_d$
(\statusknown), which avoids any exceptional-set argument.  Hence
$\log M(g,r)=O(r)$ and in particular $\tau_2(g)=\lim r^{-2}\log M(g,r)=0$.  (An earlier
version used the classical minimum-modulus theorem on circles avoiding an exceptional set
and obtained the weaker $O(r\log r)$; the conclusion $\tau_2=0$ is the same, and the
Nevanlinna route is both stronger and cleaner.)
\end{proof}

Combining Proposition~\ref{camp:prop-order} with Pila's theorem in the specialization
$a=\log2$, $b=\log3$, $\alpha=1$, $\gamma=\beta$ gives a conditional \emph{gap}.

\begin{theorem}[Conditional type gap]\label{camp:thm-typegap}
Assume Conjecture~\ref{conj:AE} fails, with canonical generator $\beta$.  Then no entire
function $g$ that is integer-valued on $\Sol$ satisfies
\[
 0<\tau_2(g)\le\frac1{832\,\beta^2\log2\log3}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
If $\tau_2(g)$ were at most the threshold, Pila's theorem would make $g$ algebraically
dependent with $2^z$ and $3^z$, whence $\tau_2(g)=0$ by
Proposition~\ref{camp:prop-order} --- contradicting $\tau_2(g)>0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{target}[Small-type integer-valued interpolant]\label{camp:target-construct}
Exhibit an entire function $g$, integer-valued on $\Sol$, with
$0<\tau_2(g)\le1/(832\beta^2\log2\log3)$, constructed from data available under a
hypothetical counterexample.  By Theorem~\ref{camp:thm-typegap} any such construction
\emph{proves} Conjecture~\ref{conj:AE}.
\end{target}

Two features make this the most attractive of the surviving targets.  First, it is
\emph{control-clean in the strong sense}: the quadratic density
$\#(\Sol\cap[0,T])=T^2/(2\beta)+O(T)$ is the exact signature of the least-generator monoid,
so at an integer control $\Sol=\N_0$ has \emph{linear} density and the entire quadratic-type
analysis is vacuous.  The route therefore consumes channel~(ii) of the control principle
(Section~\ref{log:control}) --- which most of the corpus's machinery does not.  Second, it
converts an open-ended search into a single explicit inequality.  What is ruled out is the \emph{vanishing} construction, by the finite margin of
\eqref{camp:eq-pila}: such a function has $\tau_2\ge1/(4\beta)$, which exceeds the
threshold by $208\beta\log2\log3$.  The margin is finite, not infinite --- the symmetrised
product of Proposition~\ref{camp:prop-inftype} shows $\tau_2=\pi/(2\beta)$ is achievable ---
so the vanishing branch is excluded but the achievable spectrum is \emph{not} confined to
$\{0\}\cup\{\infty\}$.  A construction whose small type comes from controlled interpolation
rather than from zeros remains untouched, and
Theorem~\ref{camp:thm-typegap} continues to forbid the interval
$(0,1/(832\beta^2\log2\log3)]$.  \statusnew{}; Pila's theorem and the minimum-modulus input
\statusknown{}; target \statusopen.

\subsection{Literature synthesis: five clusters, and one gate measured}
\label{camp:literature}

A parallel survey of the published literature (now integrated into this report as
Section~\ref{sec:litsynth} and the sections following it) identifies five clusters bearing on the
problem, and confirms that none contains an off-the-shelf theorem: every route meets the
same terminal obstruction, a nontrivial integer relation among products of logarithms of
primes.  Its negative audit is worth recording, since each item has been proposed at some
point in this corpus: a counterexample is necessarily irrational, so results about
rational $x$ add nothing; $\{(2^t,3^t)\}$ is a transcendental arc, so
Bombieri--Masser--Zannier, Maurin and Zilber--Pink do not apply merely because orbit
points are $S$-integral; Baker theory controls linear forms with \emph{algebraic}
coefficients and not the terminal coefficients $m_p\log3-a_p\log2$, which are themselves
logarithmic; $(1-z)^{\thetaq}$ is not a $G$-function, since its coefficients are not
algebraic, so arithmetic algebraization cannot be invoked without an arithmetic
replacement; and generic rational-point counting tolerates far more points than the
compact orbit produces.

The most valuable positive lead is the closest published program: Pila's theorems on entire
functions sharing arguments of integrality apply to \emph{exactly} the semigroup forced by
a counterexample, since with $a=\log2$, $b=\log3$, $\alpha=1$, $\gamma=\beta$ the four
corner values are $2,M,3,A$ and $X_{1,\beta}=\Sol$.  In this specialization an entire $g$
integer-valued on $\Sol$ with
$\tau_2(g):=\limsup r^{-2}\log M(g,r)\le1/(832\beta^2\log2\log3)$ is algebraically
dependent on $2^z$ and $3^z$, which turns the interpolation idea into a measured target.
\emph{Dependency to be audited.}  Pila's precise hypotheses and the
constant $832$ are quoted from the survey and have not been checked against the source
here; that they must contain more than is stated is visible from the control side, where
$\Sol=\N_0$ and $g(z)=\sin(\pi z)e^{cz^2}$ is entire, integer-valued on $\Sol$, and has
$\tau_2=c$ arbitrarily small --- so some hypothesis must exclude it.  (An earlier note here claimed such a construction cannot cross to the conditional world,
citing the since-retracted infinite-type proposition; in fact it crosses, but only above
$1/(4\beta)$ by Jensen, which still exceeds Pila's threshold by
$208\beta\log2\log3$, so the gate itself is unaffected.)  Every occurrence of the factor $208\beta\log2\log3$ below is
conditional on that unaudited input --- and Section~\ref{camp:ownthreshold} removes the
dependency altogether by deriving a threshold of the same shape from the corpus's own
data.
We settle that measurement.  Any $g$ forced to be independent of $2^z,3^z$ by vanishing on
the monoid pays, by Jensen's formula against the exact density
$\#(\Sol\cap[0,T])=T^2/(2\beta)+O(T)$,
\[
 \tau_2(g)\;\ge\;\sup_{c>0}\frac{2\log c+1}{4\beta c^2}=\frac1{4\beta}
 \qquad(\text{optimum at }c=1),
\]
so the gate fails by the factor
\begin{equation}
 \frac{1/(4\beta)}{1/(832\beta^2\log2\log3)}
 =208\,\beta\log2\log3
 =158.392\ldots\times\beta,
 \label{camp:eq-pila}
\end{equation}
that is by $2217.5$ at the kernel-verified $\beta\ge14$, by $4276.6$ at the computational
$\beta>27$, and \emph{growing linearly in $\beta$} --- so every improvement of the
zero-free region makes this particular gate harder, not easier.

In fact the vanishing branch fails by an infinite margin, which is worth recording because
it is both sharper and simpler than the Jensen estimate.  The monoid has counting function
$T^2/(2\beta)+O(T)$ and \emph{all its points are real and positive}, so
$\sum_{s\in\Sol}s^{-3}$ converges while $\sum_{s\in\Sol,\,s\le r}s^{-2}$ diverges, at the
exact rate $\beta^{-1}\log r$: measured increments per doubling are $0.0719$ against
$1/\beta=0.0714$, with $\sum s^{-3}=1.20647$ at $\beta=14+\sqrt2/1000$, converged to six digits in $T$
(\path{scripts/sol_canonical_type.py}); that constant is $\beta$-dependent --- it is
$1.20628$ at $\beta=14.3178$ and $1.20321$ at $\beta=27.1$ --- and only its finiteness
matters here.  Hence the Hadamard genus equals the order, both
being $2$, with divergent coefficient sum, and the canonical product --- which has minimal
growth among all entire functions vanishing on $\Sol$ --- satisfies
$\log M(r)\asymp\beta^{-1}r^2\log r$.  Therefore:

\begin{statusbox}{\textbf{Retraction} --- vanishing does \emph{not} force infinite type}
An earlier version asserted that every entire function vanishing on all of $\Sol$ has
$\tau_2=+\infty$.  That is \emph{false}.  The error was the supporting claim that the
genus-two canonical product over $\Sol$ has minimal growth among functions vanishing on
$\Sol$: Lindel\"of's finite-type criterion at order two constrains the \emph{full} divisor,
and enlarging the divisor symmetrically \emph{cancels} the divergence, because
$(is)^{-2}=-s^{-2}$.  Explicitly,
\[
 f(z)=z^4\prod_{s\in\Sol,\ s>0}\Bigl(1-\frac{z^4}{s^4}\Bigr)
\]
is entire --- the exponent of convergence of $\Sol$ is $2$, so $\sum s^{-4}$ converges
($1.08248$ over $\Sol\cap(0,4000]$) --- vanishes on all of $\Sol$, and has every factor
maximised simultaneously at $\arg z=\pi/4$, giving
$\log M(f,r)=\sum_s\log(1+r^4/s^4)$ and hence
\[
 \tau_2(f)=\frac1\beta\int_0^\infty u\log\bigl(1+u^{-4}\bigr)\,du=\frac{\pi}{2\beta}<\infty
\]
($\int_0^\infty u\log(1+u^{-4})du=\pi/2$ exactly; the ratio $\log M(f,r)/r^2$ measured at
$r=40,80,160$ is $0.1748,0.1429,0.1273$, descending to $\pi/(2\beta)=0.11219$ at
$\beta=14+\sqrt2/1000$).
\end{statusbox}

What is true is the two-sided quantitative statement, whose lower half was already in this
report and is unaffected.

\begin{proposition}[Type of functions vanishing on the monoid]\label{camp:prop-inftype}
Every nonzero entire function vanishing on all of $\Sol$ satisfies
$\tau_2\ge1/(4\beta)$, by Jensen against the density
$\#(\Sol\cap[0,T])=T^2/(2\beta)+O(T)$.  The bound is sharp within a factor $2\pi$: the
symmetrised product above attains $\tau_2=\pi/(2\beta)$.
\end{proposition}

So no function that is independent of $2^z,3^z$ by virtue of vanishing on the monoid comes
within any finite factor of Pila's threshold, and \eqref{camp:eq-pila} is merely the
elementary shadow of this.

Proposition~\ref{camp:prop-inftype} has an immediate consequence which is of independent
interest, because it says the conditional monoid is a \emph{uniqueness set} for the whole
finite-type class.

\begin{statusbox}{\textbf{Retraction} --- $\Sol$ is not a uniqueness set for finite type}
The monoid-rigidity corollary drawn from the retracted proposition --- that two entire
functions of finite quadratic type agreeing on $\Sol$ must agree identically --- falls with
it, and is false for the same witness: $f(z)=z^4\prod_{s>0}(1-z^4/s^4)$ is nonzero, of
finite type $\pi/(2\beta)$, and vanishes on all of $\Sol$, so $f$ and $0$ agree on $\Sol$
without being equal.  Evaluation on $\Sol$ is therefore \emph{not} injective on the
finite-type class, and every statement below that used injectivity is withdrawn.
\end{statusbox}

Writing $V_\tau$ for the set of entire functions that are integer-valued on $\Sol$ and have
$\tau_2\le\tau$, the situation after the retractions above is this.  $V_0$ contains every
$\Z$-polynomial in $2^z$ and $3^z$; the type gap (Theorem~\ref{camp:thm-typegap}) says
$V_{1/(832\beta^2\log2\log3)}=V_0$; evaluation on $\Sol$ is \emph{not} injective on
$\bigcup_{\tau<\infty}V_\tau$, the symmetrised product of
Proposition~\ref{camp:prop-inftype} vanishing on $\Sol$ with finite type $\pi/(2\beta)$;
and the achievable spectrum is \emph{not} $\{0\}\cup\{\infty\}$ --- in the branch where $M$
is three-smooth it contains $\log2$, by the correction in
Section~\ref{camp:diffmodule}.  What survives as the sharp open question is narrower and
better posed: the spectrum is an additive sub-semigroup of $[0,\infty]$ containing $0$ and
$\infty$, avoiding $(0,\tau_{\mathrm{crit}}]$ by the type gap, containing $\N\log2$ in the
$M$-smooth branch (and $\N\log3$ in the $A$-smooth branch), and \emph{completely unknown on
the interval $(\tau_{\mathrm{crit}},(\log2)/2)$ in every branch}.  Deciding whether that
interval is empty is what would close Target~\ref{camp:target-construct} negatively.
\statusnew.  \statusnew{}; the divergence rate \statusexactcomp.  \statusnew{}.  \emph{Erratum on the numerical check.}  The ratios $1.219,1.109,1.054$
quoted earlier were computed at $\beta=14$ --- an \emph{integer}, hence a control, where
$\Sol$ collapses to $\N_0$ and the quadratic density fails --- and over the pair multiset
rather than the point set.  At an admissible irrational $\beta$ the two coincide and the
figures are correct: recomputed at $\beta=14+\sqrt2/1000$ the ratios are
$1.2193,1.1086,1.0540,1.0269$ at $T=140,280,560,1120$, and at $\beta=14.3178$ they are
$1.2244,1.1110,1.0552,1.0275$ --- converging to $1$ from above, so the bound is valid and
slightly conservative.  At the control $\beta=14$ itself the true ratios instead tend to
zero ($0.390,0.197,0.099,0.050$), exactly as the degeneration of the density predicts.  The remaining way to use Pila's theorem therefore requires small type produced by
controlled interpolation rather than by zeros; transcendence itself is then automatic, and
the precise statement is the conditional type gap of Theorem~\ref{camp:thm-typegap} with
its construction target~\ref{camp:target-construct}.  The survey's other four clusters
--- arithmetic holonomy for products of logarithms (Calegari--Dimitrov--Tang, which
notably does \emph{not} cover $\log2\log3$ and must not be quoted as if it did),
multivariate and adelic generalized factorials, global determinant architecture
(Heath-Brown, Salberger, Walsh), and conjugate control via Schinzel--Zassenhaus and
transfinite diameter --- are templates and mechanisms rather than plug-ins, and are
recorded there with the concrete stop conditions the survey supplies.

\emph{Assessment of the campaign.}  Two of the five frontier targets are now closed as
methods (two-parameter transport, adelic wedge), one is revealed to be a restatement of
the conjecture rather than a foothold (Kummer orbit), one is exactly calibrated as a
zero-free-region generator with a measured and unfavourable dictionary (trap
architecture), and the literature's closest published program has had its single numerical
gate measured and found to fail by a linearly growing factor.  Nothing here moves the
four-exponentials barrier.  What the campaign buys is precision: the surviving frontier is
now two routes with \emph{proven sufficient conditions} --- the certified sparse near-curve
search ($\mathrm{Cap}_L=o(L)$, verification finite) and the small-type integer-valued
interpolant of Target~\ref{camp:target-construct}, which is moreover control-clean through
the monoid's quadratic density --- together with the two output-sensitive cancellation
targets (Sections~\ref{sec:masks}, \ref{bh:localized}) that have survived every campaign so
far.  Of these the interpolant target is the sharpest, being a single explicit inequality
whose satisfaction would settle the conjecture outright.  Alongside them sits the
weight-two encoding of Proposition~\ref{camp:prop-cdt}, which is the only target that
attacks the terminal obstruction head-on rather than routing around it, and which reduces
it --- for each prime $q$ separately --- to a finite independence statement inside the one
family where products of two logarithms have ever been controlled.

\section{Tangent geometry of the near-unit orbit: the shared-face mask target closes}
\label{sec:tangent}

An external report attacks the shared structural-face mask program
(Target~\ref{masks:target}) --- one of the two output-sensitive cancellation targets that
had survived every campaign in this report --- and closes its principal branches.  The
setting is the near-unit orbit: for a counterexample with $\thetaq$-convergents $p_k/q_k$,
put $z_k=2^{p_k}/M^{q_k}$ (and its companions), and for each support prime $\ell\mid MA$
let $u_{\ell,k}=v_\ell(z_k)$ be the local depth.

\subsection{Unimodular transport and the fixed cross-ratio}
\label{tg:transport}

The local depth vectors of two consecutive convergents are related by an \emph{integral
unimodular} change of basis: $(u_{\ell,k},u_{\ell,k+1})=(m_\ell,n_\ell)B_k$ with
$B_k=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}-p_k&-p_{k+1}\\q_k&q_{k+1}\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ and
$\det B_k=\varepsilon_k=\pm1$.  Everything invariant under $\operatorname{GL}_2(\Z)$ is therefore
constant along the orbit: the consecutive local gcd
$\gcd(u_{\ell,k},u_{\ell,k+1})=\gcd(m_\ell,n_\ell)=h_\ell$; the entire Smith normal form,
hence every determinantal divisor and every mod-$p$ rank; and the cross-prime determinant
$u_{\ell,k}u_{r,k+1}-u_{\ell,k+1}u_{r,k}=\varepsilon_k(m_\ell n_r-n_\ell m_r)$.  The
elementary transport identities of Section~\ref{sec:masks} are the $2\times2$ shadow of
this.

The consequence that drives everything else is a \emph{fixed} rational constant attached to
each stable denominator prime.  With the primitive tangent $(a_{\ell,k},-b_{\ell,k})$,
\[
 \frac{z_k^{\,a_{\ell,k}}}{z_{k+1}^{\,b_{\ell,k}}}=C_\ell^{\varepsilon_k},
 \qquad v_\ell(C_\ell)=0,\quad C_\ell>1,
\]
with $C_\ell$ independent of $k$: the tangent direction rotates with the convergents, but
the value along it does not move.  Since $a_{\ell,k}\sim(\gamma_\ell/h_\ell)q_{k+1}$ and
$b_{\ell,k}\sim(\gamma_\ell/h_\ell)q_k$, the tangent is \emph{linearly long} in the
convergent denominators.

\subsection{The linear-width face tax, and what it retires}
\label{tg:facetax}

Two monomials of a mask have equal $\ell$-adic pole weight exactly when their exponent
difference is an integer multiple of the primitive tangent.  Hence any nondegenerate tied
face of a bidegree-$(d,e)$ mask satisfies $d\ge a_{\ell,k}$, $e\ge b_{\ell,k}$, and
\[
 d+e\;\ge\;\frac{\gamma_\ell}{2h_\ell}\bigl(q_k+q_{k+1}\bigr),
\]
and with $R$ distinct tied prime slopes the widths add (a \emph{perimeter tax}
$d+e\ge\sum_iL_i(a_{\ell_i,k}+b_{\ell_i,k})$).  Immediately:

\begin{theorem}[Sublinear masks have no shared structural face]\label{tg:thm-nofaces}
If $d_k+e_k=o(q_k)$ then, for every stable denominator prime $\ell$ and all large $k$, the
$\ell$-adic exposed face of the mask is a \emph{single monomial}.
\end{theorem}

Five branches of the mask program are thereby retired.  \emph{Fixed or sublinear total
degree} is dead outright by Theorem~\ref{tg:thm-nofaces}: any such construction is
coefficient-driven from the start, with no geometry to exploit.  \emph{A single prime
supplying geometric cancellation} is dead by an exact edge evaluation
$E=z_k^{i_0}z_{k+1}^{j_0}P(C_\ell^{\varepsilon_k})$: a tied edge either contributes only
the bounded rational value $P(C_\ell^{\pm1})$, or contains the exact tangent binomial and
can be divided out --- and a canonical normal form performs that division, showing
\emph{one-prime geometric capture is quotient-trivial} (every mask has a representative
with no tied $\ell$-adic face, the same local value up to an $\ell$-adic unit, and explicit
height cost $H(C_\ell)^T$).  \emph{Area-only Newton-polygon arguments} are dead because the
cross-prime tangent determinant is constant in $k$, so arbitrarily long tangent pairs
coexist with bounded determinant and the polygon can be arbitrarily thin --- any bound
resting on area, mixed volume, or vertex count misses exactly the critical configurations.
\emph{Prime-count independence} fails: a Pl\"ucker syzygy
$C_\ell^{[r,s]}C_r^{[s,\ell]}C_s^{[\ell,r]}=1$ forces the tangent constants to have
multiplicative rank at most two, so additional support primes yield no additional
independent rational evaluations.  And \emph{a new irrationality measure from local depth
ratios} is illusory: those ratios are fractional-linear transforms of $\thetaq$ carrying the
same convergents, so Baker-type bounds for them are equivalent in strength to bounds for the
original pair of logarithms.

\subsection{What survives, and the weight barrier again}
\label{tg:survives}

After one-prime reduction a mask can still compress denominators in three ways: large
structural-prime divisibility in the normal-form coefficients; deep output-specific
congruences among units of different normal-form monomials; or --- the new focal point ---
\emph{interaction} between the reductions demanded by two or more nonproportional prime
slopes, a coefficient being expensive in one local basis and cheap in another.  The tangent
lattice $\Z t_{\ell,k}+\Z t_{r,k}$ has index $|\Delta_{\ell r}|$ \emph{independent of $k$},
so simultaneous reduction has only finitely many exponent residue classes; but the basis is
ill-conditioned at order $q_k$, and the rational multipliers are exactly large enough to
absorb the apparent saving.  A proof or a definitive no-go must control that coefficient
transformation place by place.  \statusopen.

The report also confirms, from its own direction, the weight diagnosis of
Section~\ref{camp:kummer}: the tangent constants do not lower the weight, since
$\log C_\ell$ is a rational-linear expression in $\log M,\log A$ and ratios of those are
fractional-linear in $\thetaq$; Baker--W\"ustholz and Laurent--Mignotte--Nesterenko remain
weight-one tools.  Its normal form is nevertheless useful as \emph{preprocessing} for
sparse-polynomial (matrix-coefficient) approaches: monomials in one tangent coset are
redundant at the evaluation point, so reducing modulo the tangent binomials separates true
support count from coefficient height exactly.  \statusnew{} throughout this section.

\emph{Assessment.}  This is the strongest negative result the mask program has received.  It
does not touch the conjecture --- every statement is $\operatorname{GL}_2(\Z)$-invariant and holds for the
controls --- but Target~\ref{masks:target}, which had survived every previous campaign, is
now reduced from ``find a shared structural face'' to the single sharply posed question of
cross-prime coefficient interaction on an ill-conditioned tangent basis.

\section{The staircase lattice, a rank-six holonomy, and the Kummer supernorm}
\label{sec:staircase}

A second external report attacks the weight-two obstruction directly and produces three
things this report can use: an exact lattice description of the $q$-smooth encoding, a
genuine \emph{holonomic} realization of the terminal relation, and a Kummer norm cocycle
with superexponential decay together with a precise reason it is not yet a proof.

\subsection{The uniform staircase lattice}
\label{st:lattice}

Working in telescoping coordinates on the consecutive logarithms, the report defines an
integral coefficient map $T_q$ and proves: $\ker T_q=\Z\cdot(e_{a_2}+e_{b_3})$ --- the only
formal invisibility is $(M,A)\mapsto(2^tM,3^tA)$, i.e.\ exactly the control direction;
$\rank T_q=2\pi(q)-1$; the image is a \emph{saturated} sublattice; and every nonzero
invariant factor of the Smith normal form equals $1$.  This is the same object as the
corrected weight-two encoding of Section~\ref{camp:cdt}, independently derived, and it
matches it numerically: the rank $2\pi(q)-1$ is precisely the count of distinct products
$\{\log2\log p\}\cup\{\log3\log p\}$ found there, and the kernel is the control line found
there.  The added value is saturation and the trivial Smith form, which remove all
algebraic ambiguity: a prime-jump tomography describes membership in the image by
constancy conditions across composite stretches, and yields a clean finite criterion ---
\emph{there is no noncontrol $q$-smooth counterexample if and only if the only vector of
the saturated cone annihilating the period vector is zero}.  \statusnew{}; it converges
with, and sharpens, Proposition~\ref{camp:prop-cdt}.

\subsection{A rank-six unipotent holonomy carrying the obstruction}
\label{st:holonomy}

The report then realizes the terminal relation as a \emph{holonomy entry}.  Iterated
integrals of the consecutive logarithmic forms give a unipotent rank-six connection,
Fuchsian on $\mathbf P^1\setminus\{-1,\dots,-(q-1),\infty\}$ with integral residue
matrices, whose parallel transport $H$ from $0$ to $1$ satisfies
\[
 H_{05}=\log2\,\log A-\log3\,\log M .
\]
This is exactly the object Section~\ref{camp:cdt} asked for: an arithmetic holonomic family
carrying the weight-two obstruction, with the finite rank and integrality that
Calegari--Dimitrov--Tang technology consumes.  It does not by itself supply the
transcendence input --- the report is explicit that the missing statement is nonvanishing
of $\mathbf{c}\cdot\mathbf{P}_q$ for primitive $\mathbf{c}$ in the saturated cone --- but it converts
``can the lattice be encoded holonomically?'' from a question into a construction.
\statusnew{}; the nonvanishing target \statusopen.

\subsection{The diagonal Kummer supernorm, and why it stops}
\label{st:supernorm}

The third contribution is a determinant cocycle $\Xi_N$ with third-order distinguished
contact, $\Xi_N=\tfrac{\beta(\beta-1)ab(a-b)}{2N^3}+O(N^{-4})$, whose diagonal Kummer norm
telescopes exactly:
\[
 \Delta_N=\prod_{\zeta^N=1}\Xi_N(\zeta)=R_N^N-S_N^N,
\]
an algebraic integer with
$\log|\Delta_N|=-N\log N+N\log|c|-\log N+O(1)$ --- decaying faster than $C^{-N}$ for every
fixed $C$.  A nonzero algebraic integer decaying superexponentially is the classic shape of
a contradiction, and the report is scrupulous about why it is not one.  Two obstructions are
identified and quantified.  A \emph{partial-norm ceiling}: contact along a proper phase
subgroup of size $N^d$ with $d<\rho$ gives at best
$\exp(-rN^d\log N+O(N^d))$ against conjugates of size $C^{N^d}$ over $N^{\rho-d}$
embeddings, and $N^d\log N=o(N^\rho)$, so polynomial contact along a proper subgroup cannot
close the product formula.  And \emph{positive phase entropy}: the leading phase symbol has
Mahler measure $m(F)\approx0.54807>0$, so the non-distinguished embeddings are exponentially
large; cyclotomic units cannot erase this, since erasing it would require the symbol to be a
product of cyclotomic polynomials in monomials, which it is not.  The resulting target ---
construct a control-sensitive cocycle whose leading phase symbol \emph{is} cyclotomic while
its first noncyclotomic Taylor coefficient is a nonzero decoded prime jump --- is recorded
as \statusopen.

\subsection{Convergence with this report's own findings}
\label{st:convergence}

Three independent confirmations are worth recording, because they were reached by different
routes.  The report's audit of small-type entire interpolation reaches exactly
Proposition~\ref{camp:prop-inftype}: canonical products vanishing on the semigroup have
infinite quadratic type, and Barnes double-gamma and double-sine constructions inherit the
same boundary-density cost.  It adds an obstruction this report had not isolated: a
zero-free Newton-series construction is blocked by the inverse of the \emph{near-collision
Vandermonde} matrix, small gaps in $\N_0+\beta\N_0$ forcing coefficient growth at exactly
the critical order --- so no subcritical construction was obtained from that direction
either.  Its lattice theorem confirms the rank $2\pi(q)-1$ and the control kernel of
Section~\ref{camp:cdt}.  And its weight analysis independently reproduces the weight-two
versus weight-one diagnosis of Section~\ref{camp:kummer}.

\emph{Assessment.}  Between them the two reports close the shared-face mask target's main
branches and supply the holonomic realization that the weight-two route needed, while
confirming three of this report's own conclusions from independent directions.  Neither
moves the four-exponentials barrier, and both say so.  The frontier after this merge is
narrower and better posed: cross-prime coefficient interaction on the tangent lattice
(Section~\ref{tg:survives}), nonvanishing of the saturated staircase pairing
(Section~\ref{st:lattice}), and a zero-entropy Kummer cocycle
(Section~\ref{st:supernorm}) --- alongside the interpolation and certificate targets of
Section~\ref{sec:campaign}.

\section{The exact type theory of the solution monoid}
\label{sec:typetheory}

An external report supplies the complete and correct theory of exactly the area in which
this report made, and has now retracted, two errors (Sections~\ref{camp:typegap},
\ref{camp:ownthreshold}).  It confirms the counterexample that forced those retractions,
identifies it as \emph{extremal}, and repairs the corollary that fell with them.

\subsection{The sharp zero-set threshold}
\label{tt:threshold}

Write $\Cbeta:=\pi/(2\beta)$.  The one-ray canonical product over $\Sol$ does have infinite
quadratic type --- along the negative axis $\log|P_\beta(-r)|\ge d_\beta r^2\log r-O(r^2)$
--- which is what this report proved and then over-generalised.  The correct object is the
\emph{rotational} product
\[
 H_{m,\beta}(z)=z\prod_{s\in\Sol\setminus\{0\}}\Bigl(1-\frac{z^m}{s^m}\Bigr),
 \qquad
 \tau_2(H_{m,\beta})=\frac{\pi}{2\beta\sin(2\pi/m)},
\]
whose type is minimised \emph{uniquely} at $m=4$, giving $\tau_2(H_\beta)=\Cbeta$.  This is
precisely the witness that refuted Proposition~\ref{camp:prop-inftype}, now seen to be
optimal rather than merely available: the fourth powers are not an accident but the
minimiser of $\csc(2\pi/m)$.

\begin{theorem}[Sharp quadratic zero-set threshold]\label{tt:thm-sharp}
If $f\not\equiv0$ is entire, vanishes on all of $\Sol$, and has $\tau_2(f)<\infty$, then
$\tau_2(f)\ge\Cbeta=\pi/(2\beta)$, and the constant is attained by $H_\beta$.
\end{theorem}

The proof is a quadratic Carlson--Carleman theorem: any discrete $A\subset(0,\infty)$ with
$\#(A\cap(0,r])=dr^2+o(r^2)$ forces $\tau_2(f)\ge\pi d$ for a nonzero entire $f$ vanishing
on $A$, applied with $d=d_\beta=1/(2\beta)$.  Two consequences repair this report directly.

\begin{corollary}[Subcritical uniqueness --- the repaired rigidity]\label{tt:cor-uniq}
If $\tau_2(f),\tau_2(g)<\Cbeta$ and $f=g$ on $\Sol$, then $f\equiv g$.
\end{corollary}

That is the correct form of the retracted Corollary~``monoid rigidity'': $\Sol$ \emph{is} a
uniqueness set, not for the whole finite-type class, but for the subcritical class
$\tau_2<\pi/(2\beta)$.  The retraction stands; the statement is recovered with the right
threshold.  Likewise the Jensen bound $1/(4\beta)$ of Proposition~\ref{camp:prop-inftype}
is superseded: the sharp constant is $\pi/(2\beta)$, larger by exactly $2\pi$, which is the
factor this report had already identified as the gap between its bound and the witness.

\subsection{The exact spectra}
\label{tt:spectra}

Both spectra are then determined.  The \emph{vanishing} spectrum is exactly
$[\Cbeta,\infty)$: every type at or above $\pi/(2\beta)$ occurs, realised by
$H_{\beta,a}=\exp(-iaz^2)H_\beta$ with $\tau_2=\Cbeta+a$, and nothing below it occurs at
all.  For the \emph{integer-valued} spectrum $\Tclass_\beta$,
\[
 \{0\}\cup[\Cbeta,\infty)\subseteq\Tclass_\beta,
 \qquad
 g_\tau(z)=2^z+\exp\bigl(-i(\tau-\Cbeta)z^2\bigr)H_\beta(z)
\]
being an explicit representative for each $\tau\ge\Cbeta$.  Combining with Pila's threshold
$\TP=1/(832\beta^2\log2\log3)$ and the fact that algebraic dependence forces $\tau_2=0$:

\begin{corollary}[The true unresolved interval]\label{tt:cor-interval}
Conditional on a counterexample,
$\Tclass_\beta\cap(0,\TP]=\varnothing$ and $[\Cbeta,\infty)\subseteq\Tclass_\beta$, so the
only unknown finite positive types lie in
\[
 \Bigl(\frac1{832\beta^2\log2\log3},\ \frac{\pi}{2\beta}\Bigr).
\]
\end{corollary}

This replaces the interval $(\tau_{\mathrm{crit}},(\log2)/2)$ recorded earlier in
Section~\ref{camp:typegap} by a strictly smaller one --- $\pi/(2\beta)=0.1122$ against
$(\log2)/2=0.3466$ at $\beta=14$ --- and it does so unconditionally on the branch structure,
whereas the earlier bound depended on the three-smooth branch.  A methodological corollary
is worth recording because it closes a natural repair strategy: \emph{adding a null function
to an interpolant cannot preserve any type bound below $\Cbeta$}, since a nonzero vanisher
already costs $\Cbeta$.  So one cannot fix a too-large interpolant by subtracting off its
error on $\Sol$.

\subsection{Covering inequalities}
\label{tt:covers}

The same Carleman input yields cover bounds that constrain \emph{families}, not just single
functions.  If $h_1,\dots,h_K$ are nonzero entire of finite types $\tau_j$ and their real
zero sets together contain $\Sol$, then $\Cbeta\le\sum_j\tau_j$; with multiplicity $q$ at
every point, $q\Cbeta\le\sum_j\tau_j$.  More strikingly, a \emph{template} form: if
$g,F_1,\dots,F_K$ have finite type, $g\not\equiv F_j$, and $g(s)\in\{F_1(s),\dots,F_K(s)\}$
for every $s\in\Sol$, then $\Cbeta\le\sum_j\max\{\tau_2(g),\tau_2(F_j)\}$; in particular if
all $F_j$ have type zero then $K\tau_2(g)\ge\Cbeta$.  This is the quantitative reason a
small-type interpolant cannot be assembled piecewise from finitely many cheap templates.
\statusnew{} throughout this section.

\section{Prime-necklace levels and projective symmetrization}
\label{sec:necklace}

Two further reports contribute exact finite structures.

\subsection{The universal signed defect and the smooth levels}
\label{nk:defect}

The prime-necklace transform attaches to a prime power an integer
$\mathcal Q_{\ell,m}(T)$, and the associated defect $\Delta_{\ell,m}$ turns out to depend on
$(\ell,m)$ \emph{only} through $h=(\ell-1)m$ --- an archimedean universality.  Writing
$t=2^{-h}$ and $G_x(u)=\log(1-u^x)-x\log(1-u)$, one has
$\Delta_h=G_x(t)-G_x(t^{\thetaq})$, and the exact integral representation
\[
 \Delta_h=x\int_{t^{\thetaq}}^{t}\frac{1-u^{x-1}}{(1-u)(1-u^x)}\,du>0
\]
gives strict positivity with $\Delta_h\sim x\,2^{-h}$, hence rational approximations
$x_{\ell,m}=v_{\ell,m}/u_{\ell,m}$ that strictly underestimate $x$ with exponentially small
error $\Delta_h/u_{\ell,m}$, and an exact signed determinant
$\det\mathbf L_{\ell,m}=-(\log3-\log2)\Delta_h<0$.

The arithmetic payoff is a finite classification: the reduced ratio
$R_h=(3^h-1)/(2^h-1)$ is $\{2,3\}$-smooth exactly for $h\in\{1,2,4\}$, with
$R_1=2$, $R_2=8/3$, $R_4=16/3$, yielding exactly six smooth prime-necklace packages
$(\ell,m)\in\{(2,1),(2,2),(3,1),(2,4),(3,2),(5,1)\}$.  The finite core is kernel-verified in
